News.title: Murder probe after man found dead as cops discover body that had been ‘lying in house for days’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

DEATH RIDDLE Murder probe after man found dead as cops discover body that had been ‘lying in house for days’

A BODY of a man has been found as cops launch a murder investigation.

The man, believed to be in his 50s, had been lying in a Northampton property for days before the grim discovery was made.

Cops rushed to a home in Burton Latimer after they received a call for a welfare check.

Sadly, a man’s body was found at the property.





Cops believe he had passed away a number of days prior to their arrival.

The body was taken to Leicester Royal Infirmary for a forensic postmortem examination.

A murder investigation has since been launched, with detectives from the East Midlands Special Operations Unit leading the probe.

Detective Inspector Cheryl Thompson said: “We’re in the early stages of establishing how the gentleman died and I would appeal for anyone in the High Street area of Burton Latimer and who may have witnessed any suspicious activity in the last week to please contact us as a matter of emergency.”

Cops have urged witnesses or anyone with information to contact Northamptonshire Police via their online portal or by calling on 101.

You can also call the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555111.

Please quote incident number 26000526485 when providing any information to make sure it gets to the right person as quickly as possible.

News.title: Fury as human poo and rotting maggot-infested food left behind at beloved UK beauty spot
News.content:
VILE CAMPERS Fury as human poo and rotting maggot-infested food left behind at beloved UK beauty spot

A HUMAN poo and maggot-infested food were left behind at a beauty spot in south Wales amid a surge in littering over the summer.

Bannau Brycheiniog National Park, also known as the Brecon Beacons, said it had noticed a recent increase in litter dumping and urged visitors to leave only footprints.



The park authority said there is “no justification” but “unfortunately, across this summer, it’s not been unusual.”

The waste left near Llyn y Fan Fawr over the bank holiday was “one of the worst” the park had seen it added.



In a post to social media the authority said: “This is not wild camping. This is fly-tipping and littering.

“One of our wardens spent their bank holiday weekend in a less-than-ideal way, clearing up a tent full of kit with chairs, a BBQ and two bags of maggot-infested food, and also found human excrement on site.



“When out enjoying nature, respect your surroundings. Leave no trace and take everything back home with you. There is no justification for this behaviour.”

Bronwyn Larry, head of communications for the park authority, said there has been an increasing number of “abandoned wild camps”.



She added: “People come to the area to enjoy the beautiful scenery, the beautiful views, but now we are being faced with litter and it’s disturbing that beautiful view.”

The authority are struggling to get through to visitors about the issue she said.

Bronwyn said the weekend’s litter was “one of the worst examples that we have come across”, but rotting food, discarded BBQs and beer cans are not uncommon.

Following a summer of wildfires the levels of littering is a growing concern.

Last month a fire raged across the park’s moorland for days in a major incident.



“Our wardens have gone from supporting firefighters with the wildfires and, the first rainy weekend, they’re off finding abandoned wild camps. They have had quite the summer,” Bronwyn said.

“It has a knock-on effect on wildlife. There’s still a fire risk. Pollution can contaminate water. It affects everything, not just it looking nice.”

Steffan Edwards, a warden at the park, told BBC Radio Wales: “We’ve got plenty of things to get on with within the national park as warden’s.”

He continued: “This isn’t new to us and it’s not new to other national parks and other beauty sites across Wales and the UK. But what we are finding is it’s an increasing problem over the last couple of years.

“People are finding out about these nice places and taking literally everything up with them, which you would take to a campsite and just leaving it there.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Policy and Advocacy Manager at Wildlife Trust Wales, Joe Wilkins, said after a summer of fires and extreme heat the wildlife “can’t sustain another threat”.

He added that it is “unfair” for some people to “absolutely ruin” the spaces for other visitors.

News.title: Third worker pulled ALIVE from Nepal tunnel and woman rescued from house 10 days after devastating floods hit region
News.content:
A THIRD worker has miraculously been pulled alive from a tunnel in Nepal 10 days after catastrophic floods devastated the country.

The Chinese national was rescued from a hydropower tunnel in the Rasuwa district, bringing the total to three workers recovered from the Trishuli project.



Two Nepalese workers were plucked from the Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel on Friday.

The third man had been trapped underground for more than ten days before emergency crews found him.



Shocking photos show the man covered in mud, drinking from a water bottle after having been stuck down a 738ft tunnel.

He was then evacuated by helicopter, with an army medic checking on him during the flight.

At least 1,259 people were killed in flash floods that struck along the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, with more than 5,000 still missing.

In flood-hit Nuwakot town, a woman was also rescued alive from a house, Nepal’s army spokesperson said.



Officials said she was being airlifted to Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal.

About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects across Nepal, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in various tunnels, authorities said.

At about 2am on Monday, a controlled blast was carried out at the Trishuli 3A hydropower site in an attempt to reach those trapped.

Nepal’s communication minister Bikram Timilsina previously said officials remain hopeful more will be recovered alive.

Large boulders and flood waters overwhelmed many of the tunnels, blocking off entrances and burying them deep in mud.



It took rescue crews six days to find the tunnels at the Trishuli facility.

News.title: Mum ‘hanged her son, 2,’ just hours after discussing Lindsay Clancy case with friends – as she’s charged with murder
News.content:
A MUM hanged her two-year-old son just hours after discussing the Lindsay Clancy case with her pals, it is alleged.

Corie Walsh, 38, has been charged with murder after her child was found hanging in the basement of her Illinois home on Tuesday.



Walsh allegedly told cops she “did this to her baby because he was the ‘devil’ and the ‘anti-Christ”, Fox 32 reports citing court documents.

After making the grim discovery, the neighbour called 911 and told operators the little boy had no pulse as she was administering CPR.



Emergency responders pronounced the child dead at the scene.

An autopsy later confirmed his death was caused by asphyxiation “due to ligature compression of the neck”, according to court documents.

Walsh was reportedly found lying in a bathtub, fully clothed and drenched in bloody water.

She was hospitalized after police determined she had attempted to self-harm, according to a court proffer seen by Fox 32.



Later in hospital Walsh admitted to cops how she committed the horror act on her child, the outlet reports.

An infant and two school-aged children were inside the home at the time the child was discovered, prosecutors said. All three remained unharmed.

Prosecutors claim Walsh had become “invested” in the Clancy murder trial.

She had reportedly been texting friends about the case in a group chat just three hours before her child was found dead.

Clancy strangled her three children to death in the basement of her Massachusetts home in January 2023.



The 36-year-old admitted to killing five-year-old Cora, three-year-old Dawson and eight-month-old Callan, but sought an insanity defense in her case.

Clancy’s defense maintains that she was suffering from severe mental illness and postpartum psychosis at the time of the attacks.

After a gruelling six-week murder case, Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial on Friday afternoon when jurors said for a third time they had failed to reach a unanimous verdict.



This means she was neither acquitted or convicted, and could be tried again in the future.

Court will resume to discuss the further legal proceedings on September 29.

As with Clancy’s defense, Walsh’s lawyer said her client was suffering “psychotic episode”.

Walsh’s husband was reportedly out of the state when the alleged murder occurred and flew home Tuesday evening.

His wife remains in custody and is being held for medical treatment.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Once cleared by medical staff, she will be transferred to the Will County Adult Detention Facility to await a detention hearing.

An investigation into the case remains ongoing.

News.title: Urgent recall of popular homewear product bought on TikTok over ‘serious’ risk of fire
News.content:
A POPULAR homewear item has been urgently recalled in the UK over a serious risk of fire.

TikTok has recalled a batch of candle warmer lamps that were sold on its online shopping platform.

The gold covered lamp was packaged in a white box, labelled as

“Aromatherapy lamp – The fragrance of faith.”



It originated from China but was sold online via TikTok.



An update from the Office for Product Safety and Standards said: “The product presents a serious risk of fire because the plug does not meet the dimensional requirements of BS 1363 and cannot make a secure connection with the socket.

“During use, this could cause the plug to overheat and catch fire.”

You should be able to return the product and receive a full refund, even if you don’t have the receipt.

But it is always worth double checking with customer service.

It is the latest in a string of recalls, revealed by retailers this week.

Primark has urgently recalled a Primark’s 101 Dalmatians Zip Purse, after it was found to pose a serious chemical risk.

Owners of the item have been told to stop using the product immediately.



Elsewhere, three ladies handbags sold in Asda have been pulled from shop shelves after they were found to contain excessive concentrations of chemicals.

The chemicals found can also cause possible damage to the reproductive system if it is found in excess quantities.

Shoppers who have bought the affected bags have been urged to bring them back to the nearest store where they will receive a full refund.

News.title: Argentina’s Falklands threat could embolden terrorists to attack island – UK must prepare for strike, says ex-Navy chief
News.content:
ON ALERT Argentina’s Falklands threat could embolden terrorists to attack island – UK must prepare for strike, says ex-Navy chief

ARGENTINA’S threats to take the Falkland Islands is “dangerous” and the UK must be prepared in the event of a “surprise attack”, a former Navy chief has warned.

During a fiery televised speech, Argentinian President Javier Milei insisted his country would reclaim the British territory while announcing sanctions on oil companies working off the islands.



Officials have brushed off the astonishing claims as a bluff, emboldened by US President Donald Trump’s recent U-Turn of support for the UK.

But experts warn there are “sinister” motives behind the Argentinian leaders remarks.



Admiral Lord Alan West, who commanded HMS Ardent during the Falklands War, branded Milei’s claims as “extraordinary” and “outrageous”.

He told The Sun: “Veterans are very hurt – our friends and colleagues died so the Falklands were free. I lost 22 boys.

“All of us fought so successfully to recover the islands – invaded by a country when it was not theirs.

“Sadly we have very painful memories.”

Britain and Argentina waged a brief but bitter war over the territory in 1982, in which 907 people were killed – 649 Argentine soldiers, 255 British troops, and three civilians.

More than 40 years on, Milei’s rhetoric has reignited a furious battle over its sovereignty.



Lord Admiral West said: “There is no doubt over the Falkland’s self determination – they’ve made it very clear. That’s why Milei’s remarks are so unbelievable.”

In a 2013 referendum, residents of the islands voted overwhelmingly to remain a British overseas territory – with 99.8 per cent voting in favour.

Lord Admiral West thwarted any speculation that Argentina could invade, citing its depleted military power, but warned Miliei’s words are “dangerous”.



He said: “Some nationalist extremists might look at these comments and think he supports their ideology and launch a terrorist attack.”

For now the UK must ramp up intelligence coverage of Argentina and make sure it is prepared, Lord West said.

He added: “The government needs to think through plans and options if things start to change.

“We’ve got to ensure there is no surprise attack that can take Mount Pleasant air field.”

The RAF Mount Pleasant base on the east of the Falklands islands, about 33 miles southwest of the capital, is home to more than 1,000 British military personnel.



Lord Admiral West said: “This RAF base allows us to fly at relatively short notice with troops and weapons.

“If we lost that airfield then it would be a different ballgame.”

A Falkland official dismissed Milei’s rant as “nothing new”.



They told The Sun: “We have been dealing with this for years. Nothing has changed.

“Of course we are monitoring it, but we are perfectly confident in our relationship with the UK government and we have had assurances from them.”

Milei’s claim over the Falklands is more likely a strategic political bid ahead of Argentina’s elections next year, ex Nato war planner and UK intelligence officer Philip Ingram MBE said.

He told The Sun: “His popularity is flat-lining – it’s a standard tactic to try and stir up national fervor.

“But there are more sinister motivations at play.”



Geological surveys suggest that the seas around the Falklands contain several potential large oil fields, including Sea Lion.

Test drilling suggests Sea Lion could contain more than double the annual output of the entire North Sea.

Philip said: “It wasn’t initially clear how much oil was in these reserves.



“We now know its some of the largest in the world and Milei is trying to manipulate a deal out of that.”

Early reports suggested about 791million barrels of oil could be recovered, but that was upped to 917million barrels last year.

Control of the oil field currently lies between an Israeli and a British firm – with none of the profits set to reach Argentina.

During his address to the nation, a furious Milei said: “If we do not act swiftly in a few months, they will have the material capacity to access the oil that lies underneath our sea. Something that has never happened before.

“That means that our national claim is facing a clear and present danger, and requires a proportional response. We will not allow it.”



With billions of pounds at stake, the Falklands could now become a “flash point” for a number of different countries, Philip said.

“But Argentina is not a player in that fight because they have no claim to the territory”, he added.

Milei’s announcement came just hours after Trump hinted he would not back the UK if Argentina invaded the archipelago, citing the lack of support in the war on Iran.

It follows a leak of an internal Pentagon email in April implying the US may review its position on the islands.



The US has formally recognised the UK’s de facto administration of the islands but has not taken a formal position on sovereignty.

Referring to Trump’s latest stance, Milei said: “The US is considering this change of position because it knows that Argentina has a reliable partner, aligned with western values, in a strategically important position that can be a valuable ally in the decades to come.”

The UK is facing “multiple crises” that are “unlikely to be resolved” while “Argentina‘s future is flourishing and will prevail”, he added.

Furious British ministers have hit back, doubling down on Britain’s “unshakeable commitment to the Falklands”.



Defence Secretary West Streeting wrote on X: “Milei’s statement overnight tells us more about domestic politics in Argentina than it does about the Falkland Islands.

“The Falklands are British because Falkland Islanders choose to be British. Our commitment to the Falklands is absolute and unshakeable.”

Meanwhile Kemi Badenoch blasted Milei with a warning that “Britain does not surrender to bullies”.

She wrote on X: “If he wants a stronger Argentina, he should build its economy, not threaten others.

“But there’s also a lesson here for our sleepy Labour government. The madness of surrendering the Chagos Islands means other countries are now trying their luck.”



Andy Burnham is set to continue Sir Keir Starmer’s Chagos giveaway deal, the Government confirmed earlier this week.

The agreement, struck by Sir Keir last May, will cede sovereignty of the Indian Ocean archipelago to Mauritius.

Britain will pay millions of pounds a year to rent back Diego Garcia island, which hosts a joint UK-US air base, in a deal Trump branded as “a great act of stupidity”.

Philip said: “Chagos undermined British security on the World Stage. It was disastrous.”

Burnham must now prepare for Milei to bring “significant legal action over the Falklands” – which will cost the British taxpayer billions of pounds.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Philip said: “He is likely going to try and stir this up in the UN.

“And when he does Burnham will have to decide if we’re going to roll over and give it away like we did with Chagos, or set our own conditions.”

News.title: The flash Gen Z narcos sparking new wave of terror with live-stream assassinations & idiot influencers hired as henchmen
News.content:
GANG-Z The flash Gen Z narcos sparking new wave of terror with live-stream assassinations & idiot influencers hired as henchmen

LOS Rugrats – it does not conjure up the most fearsome of images.

But it is, in fact, a highly violent enforcement wing of the deadly Sinaloa Cartel, founded in Mexico by the now-jailed El Chapo and El Mayo in the 1980s.



Its alleged leader, 30-year-old drug kingpin Carlos Paez Pereda, has adopted the alias Carlitos Rugrats – a nod to the Nickelodeon cartoon but his crimes are far from child’s play.

The US Department of Justice (DoJ) has charged 5ft 7in Carlitos Rugrats – who is currently a wanted man by the FBI and the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) – with narcoterrorism, material support of terrorism, and drug trafficking “massive amounts of fentanyl, cocaine, and methamphetamine” into the USA.



In a statement announcing the charges, US Attorney Adam Gordon said: “You can’t arrest a cartoon character. But you can arrest a narco-terrorist.”

FBI Special Agent Mark Remily said the cartel’s faction, despite its name, was incredibly dangerous.



“Los Rugrats has fuelled brutal violence in Mexico that reaches into the United States along with a relentless flow of deadly drugs into our communities,” he explained.

His colleague from the DEA, Special Agent James Nunnallee, said Paez has helped fuel the drug crisis in the USA and used violence to protect his criminal enterprise.



“As alleged in the indictment, his organisation relied on murder, kidnapping, and armed enforcers to maintain power and ensure the continued flow of drugs that have devastated families and communities across our nation,” he said.

What is staggering about Rugrats’ crimes is how openly he bragged of them online.

Photos shared by the DoJ of Carlitos Rugrats’ now-locked Instagram account see blinged-up guns touted alongside emojis.

One snap shows a man wearing an holding a golden gun engraved with the name “Paez”.

In another snap, 11 guns are laid out on what looks appears to be a bed in varying shades including silver and gold.



And one picture is of three black weapons is captioned “My 3 fav” with the heart-eyes emoji.

It may be shocking but Carlitos Rugrats is just one of a number of Gen Z cartel members whose criminal careers are coliding with their social media presence.

The Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (Acled) reports 64 influencers are currently under investigation for helping criminal networks launder their profits in Mexico.

And Mexican newspaper El Universal suggests at least 19 influencers and content creators have been killed in the country since 2024.

María Fernanda Arocha from Acled has warned of “narco-influencers” – creators with large followings who showcased luxurious lifestyles and have alleged ties to criminal groups.



“While in most cases the links with criminal groups are not proven, the use of some gang symbols and ‘narcocorridos’, music glorifying the life of narcos, have been seen as a sign of support for the actions of the criminal groups,” she said.

“On top of creating content, influencers sometimes also play an important role in laundering money: there are currently 64 influencers under investigation for their alleged role in such operations.”

According to El País, the Spanish-language newspaper, the ‘ninja’ emoji is used by people who work for cartels to recruit hitmen.



The newspaper also says accounts linked to Los Chapitos, the wing of the Sinaloa Cartel associated with the sons of El Chapo, frequently used a pizza slice emoji alongside the letters “ch”.

This forms the word “chapizza” which is believed to be a reference to the faction’s nickname.

Meanwhile, the rooster emoji has appeared in content linked to the narco-terrorist organisation Cartel Jalisco Nueva Generación (CJNG) – whose leader, El Mencho, was killed by the Mexican army in February 2026. He was nicknamed “El Señor de los Gallos”, which means Lord of the Roosters. The cowboy hat emoji is thought to be linked to El Mayo – jailed for life for drug trafficking and murder in July 2026 – as he was known as “El Señor del Sombrero”, which means “The Man with the Hat.”

César Gastélum, 25, who had 600,000 followers on TikTok, was known for sporting a pale cowboy hat in his comedy videos and live streams.

He was wearing it as he was shot dead outside a KFC in Culiacán, Sinaloa, while live-streaming a prank on August 4 this year.



The attack, which was not filmed for TikTok, has been linked to cartel activity by some. So far no one has been arrested.

The murder has also drawn chilling comparisons to the killing of Mexican beauty influencer Valeria Márquez, who was also shot dead during a TikTok livestream earlier this year.

The 23-year-old was working inside her beauty salon in Zapopan, Jalisco, when a gunman entered and opened fire.



Viewers watched in horror as Márquez was reportedly shot once in the chest and twice in the head before collapsing to the floor.

Earlier in the livestream, she chillingly told followers: “Maybe they were going to kill me or something.”

Prosecutors later launched a femicide investigation into her death.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It comes after Mexican authorities announced the arrest of Ramón Ángel Álvarez Ayala, also known as “El R1,” a senior alleged figure in the CJNG, over claims he was behind the influencer’s murder.

These modern day narco influencers are not only as violent as their forefathers – they also share it on social media.

News.title: Masked protesters block roads in Dover bringing traffic to standstill as ‘all routes’ disrupted at port & in town
News.content:
LORRIES and holidaymakers are facing travel chaos at the Port of Dover as masked protesters block roads around the town.

Kent Police said officers were scrambled following the disturbance and confirmed they have been “engaging with protesters” at the scene.



Reform UK councillor John Baker, for Kent County Council, said he believes it is a “stop the boats” protest – but protesters have not confirmed this.

P&O Ferries has warned customers that access to the UK’s busiest ferry port is “restricted” amid the chaos in Kent this morning.



In a statement on X, the firm said: “Please be advised that access to the Port of Dover is currently restricted.

“If you miss your sailing, we will get you onto the next when you reach our check-in.”



Videos circulating on social media show protesters, dressed in black and wearing balaclavas, gathered around the port.

One holidaymaker told how their coach had been stopped by the group – preventing them from getting onto a France-bound ferry.

They told The Sun: “We’re on a coach in Dover being stopped from getting to our ferry over to France by protesters.



“A couple of them got hit by a car driving through them. They’re all in black and wearing masks.”

Commuter Nathan Ditchburn said the group arrived at around 6.45am.

He told KentOnline: “I would say there are around 300 men, maybe more.



“They have blocked off every entrance and exit of the Dover port area, and Jubilee Way is blocked as well.

“It will be causing huge delays for the ferries today.”

The Port of Dover described the situation as an “ongoing public order incident” and said it was working alongside Kent Police.



A statement read: “The Port of Dover can confirmed that there is an ongoing public order incident happening around the town of Dover.

“This is affecting all routes in and out of the port and the town.

“We are in contact with Kent Police to understand the situation.



“This situation is impacting our local community and our customers, so of course we are hoping for a swift resolution.”

Mike Tapp, Labour MP for Dover and Deal, blasted the group as “idiots coming to Dover to cause disruption”.

In a post on Facebook, he said: “Park run cancelled and port access disrupted.

“I am fed up with idiots coming to Dover to cause disruption.

“I bet if you asked any one of those ‘protesters’ they wouldn’t know small boat crossing are down by 40% and we are working hard to fix the mess.



“Go home, enjoy your weekend/get a job.”

National Highways confirmed the A20 is closed in both directions and warned drivers of four-mile-long queues due to “protest activity”.

Traffic has stopped moving from the Eastern Docks roundabout to the Court Wood Interchange.

It said: “A20 both directions in Kent between A256 (York Street) & A2 (Jubilee Way).

“Traffic is currently stopped due to protest activity at Dover Port.



“Current delays of up to 30 minutes on the approach, with 4 miles of congestion.”

Dover West Reform councillor Paul King said a “large number of men” had blocked the A20 and told locals to avoid the port area.

Ferry operator DFDS warned passengers of traffic disruption at the port.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It wrote: “We are aware of the current traffic disruption affecting access to the Port.

“Rest assured we will accommodate you onto the next departure once you arrive.”

News.title: Reform UK conference LIVE: Tetchy Robert Jenrick loses cool in TV interview over donations row as final day kicks off
News.content:
WATCH: Protester dragged out of Farage speech reveals why he heckled Reform leader

One of the protesters thrown out of Nigel Farage's speech said he had shouted at the party leader to highlight corruption at the heart of reform.

The heckler, named Ed, told The Mirror he is part of a group called Resist Reform.

He said: "We just stood up in the Reform conference to highlight the corruption at the heart of the Reform Party."

Asked what he shouted at Mr Farage he said: "There was quite a lot of adrenaline in the moment, so I think what I shouted was roughly, 'Are you one of these people who's corrupted by donations, Nigel?'

"I know he took £5million from Christopher Harborne, who's a big tech billionaire who doesn't even live in the country, and he's also been caught in a sting operation taking illicit funds from the USA, and seeming to know about that as well.

"So the idea was to raise people's awareness of that and to show that that's happening, because they talk a lot about nation and community values in that room.

"And I believe some of the people there are genuinely there because that's what they believe, but they should know that this is a party that will flout the rules to get into power, and that just doesn't really care about the kinds of things that would keep us as ordinary citizens that we would actually have to obey."

And he continued: "I hope that we've raised awareness of the corruption scandal that is just blowing up today, because this is something that hopefully will make people aware that Reform is not a party that can be trusted in power."

News.title: Little-known rule that can mean £100 fine and 3 penalty points when running out of petrol
News.content:
Little-known rule that can mean £100 fine and 3 penalty points when running out of petrol

Running out of fuel can not only be frustrating but can leave you with a fine and penalty points on your driving licence

View 3 Images Thousands of people run out of petrol every year (Image: Getty)

Many motorists know the feeling of driving to the petrol station as the fuel gauge falls and warning lights glow on the dashboard. However, while not only massively inconvenient, running out of fuel can also mean a £100 fine and three penalty points on your driving licence, depending on the circumstances.

Under Rule 97 of the Highway Code motorists are warned they must "have sufficient fuel or charge for your journey, especially if it includes motorway driving". Getting it wrong could prove costly for while running out of fuel isn’t itself illegal drivers can be fined a minimum of £100 and three penalty points if their car obstructs the road as a result of an avoidable breakdown or if running out of fuel results in what is ruled to be careless or dangerous driving. If a vehicle causing an obstruction is found to be at fault for a collision, the penalty can be more serious.

View 3 Images It is important to ensure you have enough fuel for your journey (Image: Getty Images)

AA figures from 2022 showed they attended more than 10,500 breakdowns as a result of members running out of fuel or electrical charge with many of these on motorways or fast-moving roads.

Speaking previously, Edmund King, AA president said: “There can be some genuine reasons for running out of fuel such as a faulty gauge or undetected fuel leak. On occasions cars may get stuck in jams for hours due to bad winter weather or miles of disruption leading to Channel ports which could result in running out of fuel. Hence we advise to always have at least one quarter of a tank of fuel. Likewise, some EV drivers might run low or out of charge if several chargers aren’t working.

“One would hope that police officers would be reasonable in those circumstances. But where drivers negligently run on fumes, leaving themselves and others in danger on the road, the weight of the law can be brought to bear on them. Don’t be a fuel gambler by running on fumes.

“Most of the out-of-fuel cases the AA sees are a result of driver misjudgement, and the police have the power to give a warning or a penalty if it is deemed to be careless driving or causes an obstruction. If you are running low, you can use the AA route planner to find the closest and cheapest fuel."

View 3 Images It is important to fill up before your car runs out of fuel (Image: Getty Images)

The RAC also had a warning for motorists. It said: "While running out of fuel isn’t illegal in itself, any careless or dangerous driving that results from it could see you punished by law. You could receive a penalty of £100 and three points on your licence if you are forced to stop in the road and cause an obstruction.

"In cases where your empty fuel tank leads to an accident, as well as putting yourself and other road users at extreme risk, you could be taken to court, or issued with 9 points and an unlimited fine."

What should I do if I run out of petrol?

According to vehicle insurance firm tempcover one of the most important things to do after running out of petrol is to ensure you stay safe. It advises:

Article continues below

As soon as it is safe to do so, pull over and turn on your hazard lights

Once parked, you should contact your breakdown service provider or a friend or family member who is able to bring you fuel in a jerry can

If you have stopped in a dangerous location or are obstructing traffic, contact the emergency services

If you’ve stopped on a motorway, leave the vehicle on the side away from the traffic and walk to a safe place. Stay near the car, but on the other side of the barrier

Don’t attempt to walk to a petrol station, especially if on a motorway

It added: "You should also try to avoid restarting the vehicle if you’re out of fuel. This is because it could cause more damage to your engine. Check your breakdown policy to see if running out of fuel is covered. Some breakdown providers may charge separately to help you get to a petrol station."

News.title: Parents of students 'could be liable' for damage caused by people they don't know
News.content:
Parents of students 'could be liable' for damage caused by people they don't know

An expert is urging parents to check the small print

View 3 Images Check the terms (Image: izusek via Getty Images)

Parents of students are being warned that they could be liable for damage caused by people they don't even know.

‌



Those agreeing to act as guarantors for teenagers moving into student houses are being warned to read the small print carefully, as they could potentially become liable for unpaid rent or damage caused by other tenants. The Renters' Rights Act, which came into effect earlier this year, stops an agent or landlord from asking for rent to be paid in advance, potentially meaning more parents, relatives and friends will be asked to act as guarantors for residential tenancies.

‌



With thousands of university students relying on a guarantor, many families may assume they are only taking financial responsibility for their own child. Tim Wakelin, founder of Guarantor Insure, warned that shared tenancy agreements could include “joint and several liability”, potentially allowing a landlord to pursue one guarantor for liabilities relating to the wider tenancy rather than simply their child's individual share.

‌



Guarantor Insure says that under such an agreement, if another tenant stops paying rent or causes damage, a landlord may be able to pursue an individual guarantor for the full amount, depending on the wording of the agreement.

View 3 Images Parents could be liable for other tenants (Image: Milky Way via Getty Images)

Tim said: “The biggest message to any parent who is asked to become a guarantor is: check the contract before you sign it. If you are joint and severally liable, then as a guarantor you could be asked to pay for damage or unpaid rent caused by the other tenants.

‌



“Parents naturally think, ‘I know my son or daughter and I trust them, so I'm happy to guarantee their rent'. What they may not appreciate is that they could potentially be signing something much wider than that.

“In a student house, you may barely know the other people your child is moving in with, never mind their financial circumstances or their guarantors. Yet depending on the agreement you've signed, their actions could potentially become your financial problem.”

Guarantor Insure says the risk was the reason the business was originally created, after its founders experienced the issue themselves while acting as guarantors for their own children's student tenancies. Its cover is designed for private individuals, guaranteeing shared student tenancies where joint and several liability applies.

‌



Its current product provides different levels of cover for student tenancy guarantors, including protection against qualifying unpaid rent and damage claims, alongside dispute resolution, legal cover and access to a legal helpline, subject to the policy terms. Tim expects the issue of guarantors to become increasingly important across the wider rental market following changes as a result of the Renters' Rights Act, including restrictions around landlords demanding large amounts of rent upfront. He believes that could result in more tenants being asked to provide a parent, relative or friend as a guarantor instead.

View 3 Images Tim Wakelin (Image: Newspage)

He added: “This isn't about telling parents they shouldn't help their children. For many students, having Mum, Dad or another family member act as guarantor is what enables them to secure the property in the first place.

Article continues below

“But signing a guarantee shouldn't be treated as a formality. You need to understand exactly what you're guaranteeing, how long that responsibility lasts and under what circumstances you could be pursued for money.

“The potential problem is that people sign because they trust the person they're helping, without necessarily appreciating that the agreement may expose them to the behaviour of everybody else sharing that tenancy. Read the agreement carefully, ask questions if you don't understand it and make sure you know the potential financial liability before putting your name on it.

“You wouldn't normally agree to guarantee the debts of a group of people you've never met without understanding the risks. A student tenancy shouldn't be treated any differently.”

News.title: Jay-Z fans distracted at London gig as they realise who's dancing wildly in crowd
News.content:
Jay-Z fans distracted at London gig as they realise who's dancing wildly in crowd

Jay-Z fans were left distracted at a recent London gig when they saw who was dancing wildly in the crowd. The unexpected moment left many onlookers totally taken aback

View 2 Images Jay-Z fans were left totally distracted (stock image) (Image: Kevin Mazur, Getty Images For Parkwood Entert)

Rap legend Jay-Z has kicked off his tour dates in London after unexpectedly popping up at a city hotspot earlier this week. However, even though thousands of fans were waiting to see the icon take to the stage, they ended up being distracted by someone completely different.

‌



When he performed in London on Friday (September 4) night, concertgoers found their attention drawn to someone else, even though he put on an epic show. Jay, 56, is also set to perform on September 5 as part of his Jay-Z 30 tour. The concerts were organised to mark the 30th anniversary of his debut album, Reasonable Doubt, alongside the 25th anniversary of his sixth album, The Blueprint and, judging by the clips that are already going viral, it's evident he's putting on a good show.

‌



However, rap fans were stunned when they spotted a woman dancing wildly in the crowd. She was clearly having the time of her life at the show, but jaws dropped when people realised who she actually was.

‌



Who did they see?

Captioning one clip, social media user Leila Ostria wrote: "I HAVE NO WORDS. WHAT ARE THE ODDS SHE'S RIGHT BEHIND ME?"

She went on to reveal that Beyonce was seated incredibly close to her throughout the performance, and she was visibly starstruck. The footage continues to show the superstar dancing away, clearly having an absolute blast.

The video has since sparked considerable conversation as more than 8,000 people have watched it since it was posted. Viewers had plenty to say after witnessing Beyonce letting loose in the crowd.

‌



One said: "I'm not used to seeing her this animated, lol. I love how much fun she is having!" Another wrote: "She is so adorable."

A third replied: "I love how she fan girls for her man! She's so cute."

Meanwhile, a fourth also commented: "I was there too and I didn't even notice her. That's crazy, but she was so happy."

‌



One more also added: "Omg, she is us, and having so much fun!"

View 2 Images Beyonce attended her husband's show (stock image) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Earlier this week, rap icon Jay-Z is reported to have left fans stunned after turning up at an immersive installation in London's Trafalgar Square. It was launched to coincide with his concerts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium this weekend.

Article continues below

The installation features period televisions showing music videos, live performances and contemporary programming. The aim is said to be transporting audiences back to 2001, while capturing the cultural significance of The Blueprint.

While fans have been beside themselves with excitement at seeing him, it's evident that few anticipated spotting him, or his wife Beyonce, at such close quarters this week. The superstar couple have clearly sent fans into a frenzy.

During Friday's show, Jay also led the crowd in singing "happy birthday" to his wife during the performance. The singer turned 45 on Friday.

News.title: 'I sell my guinea pig's paintings on Vinted - they're gone within minutes'
News.content:
'I sell my guinea pig's paintings on Vinted - they're gone within minutes'

EXCLUSIVE: The guinea pig named Cheesecake from Manchester has a long waiting list for his tiny works of art after his owner, Alexandra Greenwood, taught him to paint

I bought a painting made by a guinea pig

You never know what you'll come across when you scroll through Vinted. From clothes and accessories to homeware or collectors' items, it truly is a market hub for anything you might want and more - including rocks from various beaches.

‌



This is something I realised after coming across a handmade painting by a guinea pig called Cheesecake. Yes, you read that right. I was immediately intrigued, after learning about the artistic pet on social media, that I had to spend £5 for one of his paintings.

‌



But how did Cheesecake even get into painting in the first place?

‌



Speaking to his owner, Alexandra Greenwood from Manchester, she said that Cheesecake had always been the quickest learner out of all of her three guinea pigs, saying he often played with dog puzzle toys, and even solves them pretty quickly.

She added: "He learned how to pick up his biscuits and drop them out of his pen so that they’d fall on the floor, which I accidentally taught him would get him a treat, as whenever he’d do it and go over and give him something."

His painting skills started when Alexandra was a university student and would often study in the guinea pigs' room, with Cheesecake quickly realising if he took one of her pens, she'd pay attention to him.

‌



This lead to Cheesecake often picking up the pens and running away with them. Alexandra used this to her advantage by quickly teaching him the command for 'pick up', which she said would be a great skill when she takes photos of him. But then it led to Cheesecake starting to paint.

View 3 Images Cheesecake the guinea pig has gone viral on Vinted for his unique paintings (Image: Alexandra Greenwood)

"We started off with watercolour paint since it doesn’t stain and it doesn’t smell very strong, and he took to it really quickly!" Alexandra said. "I had to buy him his own brushes though, because he was totally ruining mine by smashing them into the paper."

‌



Alexandra started to list a few of his paintings on Vinted, selling them for £5 in a way for the guinea pig to 'earn his own pocket money' for treats and toys, while also making people smile with his artworks. While people have bought the painting's as gifts for their loved ones, there was one story that stood out to Alexandra.

"We had a really special one where a painting was bought for a family member who was in hospital as a cheer up gift and we sent a video of Cheesecake painting it along with it," she shared. "I got a message a few weeks later which was so lovely - it had really cheered up the family member and made all the nurses smile too!"

She added: "I really love that people can find joy in little things like this - for ten minutes of Cheesecake’s time, each painting seems to make such a difference."

‌



View 3 Images Alexandra Greenwood started selling her guinea pig's art on Vinted (Image: Alexandra Greenwood)

And people really seem to love them, as the paintings went viral online, making Alexandra baffled by how long his waitlist had gotten.

"I’m not quite sure how he went viral though!" Alexandra said. "I think someone may have reposted us in a Vinted group on Facebook - after that, we would get up to 20 messages a day asking for paintings, and every time I’d list one on Vinted it would honestly sell within a minute, it’s been so crazy!"

‌



Now, she said people love Cheesecake 'almost as much' as she does, as he has a long waitlist of people waiting to get their hands on one of his paintings.

"At the minute, he only makes one every couple of days because I don’t want to push him and make it something he doesn’t enjoy, but unfortunately that does mean that there’s an insanely long wait list for reserved paintings and that there’s always a scramble when I post the unreserved ones," she said.

View 3 Images Social News Reporter Alice Sjoberg showed off the painting she bought from Cheesecake and Alexandra (Image: Alice Sjoberg)

Article continues below

And he sure is making people smile, as I ended up managing to get my hands on one of my own paintings, which is now placed on my desk, making me smile every time I look at it.

News.title: Factory fined £333,000 after woman's arm broken by sausage roll machine
News.content:
Factory fined £333,000 after woman's arm broken by sausage roll machine

The company was taken to court by the Health and Safety Executive

View 3 Images David Wood Baking Limited failed to prevent access to dangerous parts of machinery

A company has been fined more than £333,000 after an employee broke her arm when it became trapped in a sausage roll machine. Ribeca Jesuthasan was working for David Wood Baking Limited at the company’s manufacturing factory in Dorset Road, Sheerness, when the incident happened.

‌



She was cleaning a sausage roll production line when she put her hand through an unguarded conveyor roller. Although it had been switched off, it began to operate while she was cleaning it and her arm was pulled into the rotating roller, causing multiple fractures and a broken arm.

‌



The accident happened on December 1, 2023, and was investigated by the Health Safety Executive (HSE), which found the company had failed to prevent access to the rotating parts of the machine. David Wood Baking Limited, of Calverley Road, Leeds, pleaded guilty to breaching Regulation 11(1) of the Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998.

‌



View 3 Images The machinery was making sausage rolls

‌



The company was fined £333,333 and ordered to pay £7,644 in costs at court. HSE guidance says employers have a legal duty to take effective measures to prevent access to dangerous parts of machinery. This will normally involve the use of fixed guarding.

Where routine access is required, interlocked guards may be necessary to prevent dangerous parts moving before a person can reach the danger zone. HSE inspector Delcina Burden said: “Too many workers are seriously injured every year as a result of contact with dangerous parts of machinery due to inadequate or absent guarding.

View 3 Images A worker suffered multiple fractures after her arm was caught in an unguarded conveyor

Article continues below

“If simple measures had been taken, this incident could have been avoided. The sentence handed down by the court in this case should demonstrate that the courts and HSE take breaches of health and safety law seriously. We will not hesitate to take action against companies that fail to do all they can to keep people safe.”

News.title: Council tax check that could reveal if you are owed money
News.content:
Council tax check that could reveal if you are owed money

It could be worth logging into your council tax account and looking at the balance to see if you have fallen into credit

View Image Check if you are in credit to your council (Image: Getty Images)

Council tax bills have climbed again this year, but before assuming all the money is heading out of your account, there is one quick check worth making to see whether some could actually be coming back.

‌



Council tax is one of those bills most of us pay without giving it much thought. The direct debit goes out every month and, unless something changes dramatically, we tend to leave it alone.

‌



But it could be worth logging into your council tax account and looking at the balance.

‌



That's because it is possible for a council tax account to fall into credit, meaning your local authority could be holding money that may be refundable to you.

There are several reasons this can happen, including moving home, overpaying, having a discount applied retrospectively or successfully having your council tax band changed.

And while some refunds happen automatically, you shouldn't assume yours will. GOV.UK advises people who have paid too much council tax and haven't received an automatic refund to contact their local council.

‌



Get the best deals and tips from Mirror Money WHATSAPP GROUP: Get money news and top deals straight to your phone by joining our Money WhatsApp group here. We also treat our community members to special offers, promotions, and adverts from us and our partners. If you don’t like our community, you can check out any time you like. If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Money newsletter here for all the best advice and shopping deals straight to your inbox.

Why could your council tax account be in credit?

One of the simplest explanations is moving house. Council tax is calculated according to your liability for a particular property. If you've already paid ahead when you move, you could end up with a credit once the final bill is calculated.

Discounts and exemptions can also be applied retrospectively. For example, someone who becomes entitled to the 25% single-person discount could find that their account is adjusted after they have already made payments.

‌



The same can happen if Council Tax Reduction is subsequently awarded or if a property's council tax band is successfully changed.

Money expert Jasmine Birtles says it's worth checking rather than assuming the figures have automatically sorted themselves out.

She said: "Council tax is one of those payments that disappears from our bank accounts every month and most of us don't look at it again.

‌



"But people's circumstances change. They move home, become entitled to discounts or have adjustments made to their bills, and that can sometimes leave an account in credit.

"It only takes a few minutes to log in and look at the balance. If you see a credit and don't understand why it's there, contact your council and ask whether you're entitled to have it refunded."

How to check

Find your latest council tax bill or log into the council tax section of your local authority's website. Look for your account balance and any recent adjustments.

‌



Don't panic if the way the balance is displayed isn't immediately obvious. Councils don't all present online accounts in exactly the same way, so contact the council tax department if you're unsure whether a figure represents a genuine credit.

If you have overpaid, GOV.UK says you should contact the council if you haven't automatically received the money back.

You can find your local authority through the Government's council finder. It's also worth checking whether you are missing a council tax discount or reduction, particularly if your household circumstances have changed.

‌



Give your bill a five-minute MOT

Don't stop at the balance. While you have the bill in front of you, check the name and address are correct, that any discount you expect is showing and that the council tax band matches the band listed for your property.

The average Band D council tax bill in England for 2026/27 is £2,392, so getting a reduction wrong can make a substantial difference over the course of a year.

The single-person discount is one of the best-known examples. If you're the only adult counted for council tax purposes in your home, you can usually get 25% off.

‌



There are other circumstances in which people may qualify for discounts, reductions or exemptions, however, so don't assume the full bill is necessarily the correct one.

Jasmine adds: "With a bill this big, I wouldn't put it completely on autopilot. I would check it at least when the new bill arrives and whenever something significant changes in the household.

"People are very good at shopping around to save £20 on something they buy, but sometimes forget to check the bills that cost them thousands of pounds a year."

‌



What about your council tax band?

You can also check that your home is in the correct council tax band. In England and Scotland, council tax bands are still based on historic property values, and it is possible to challenge your band if you have evidence suggesting it is wrong.

This is one area where you shouldn't simply fire off a challenge because you think your bill looks expensive.

Before doing anything, check how council tax band challenges work and compare your property with similar homes nearby.

‌



A challenge can result in the band being reviewed, so you need evidence rather than simply hoping for a reduction.

What happens to credit?

Having a credit showing doesn't necessarily mean the council will immediately transfer that exact amount into your bank account.

The council may need to check your account first, and outstanding council tax liabilities can affect what happens to the balance.

‌



Refund procedures also differ between local authorities.

That makes the safest approach remarkably simple: check the balance, and if it appears that the council owes you money, ask for it. And don't cancel your council tax direct debit simply because you think you've overpaid.

Council tax is a priority bill, and falling into arrears can have serious consequences. Anyone having difficulty paying should speak to their council about support rather than simply stopping payments. There is also help available if household bills are becoming unaffordable.

‌



Jasmine said: "The point isn't to stop paying anything. It's simply to check you're paying what you should be paying.

"If there is £20, £100 or more sitting in an account that you're entitled to have returned, I'd much rather see that money back in someone's bank account than forgotten about."

For once, checking a household bill might reveal something rather nicer than another price increase.
