World.title: Expanded free college law to help more Filipino youth earn degrees – Dy
World.content:
House Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy III — File photo

MANILA, Philippines — Speaker Faustino “Bojie” G. Dy III said Friday that amendments to the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act would give more Filipino students opportunities to enter college or technical-vocational training and support them in completing their education.

Dy joined President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., Senate President Sherwin “Win” T. Gatchalian, Education Secretary Juan Edgardo “Sonny” M. Angara, Commission on Higher Education Chairperson Shirley C. Agrupis, Technical Education and Skills Development Authority Secretary Jose Francisco “Kiko” B. Benitez and other congressional leaders at the ceremonial signing of Republic Act No. 12325, or the Act Enhancing the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act.

“For many families, it is not enough for their child to simply enter college. The real success is seeing them graduate, find a decent job and improve the life of the entire family,” Dy said.

Article continues after this 

Under the law, qualified students from Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program households will receive priority in the grant of tertiary education subsidies.

This will provide support for qualified 4Ps graduates admitted to government-recognized higher education and technical-vocational institutions.

RA 12325 also establishes a Private Education Assistance Program that will provide government grants to poor and deserving students pursuing priority programs in qualified private higher education institutions and technical-vocational institutions.

“When worries about transportation, books, food and other education expenses are reduced, students can focus more on their dreams. This assistance is not only for the student; it is an investment in the future of their family,” Dy said.

The Isabela lawmaker thanked House members and leaders for acting urgently on the measure, which was among the priority bills identified by the Legislative-Executive Development Advisory Council, and for working with the Senate to reconcile and pass the legislation.

Article continues after this 

“I thank our leaders and members of the House who acted promptly and united to pass this important measure. We have shown that Congress responds immediately when the future of Filipino youth is at stake,” Dy said.

Dy said Congress’ responsibility does not end with the enactment of the law, adding that the House will exercise oversight and closely monitor the formulation of its implementing rules, distribution of subsidies and concerned agencies’ compliance with its provisions.

Article continues after this 

“The House will monitor the implementation of this law to ensure that the funds reach students who truly need them properly and quickly. This law will only be meaningful when our people feel its benefits,” he said.

World.title: Sara Duterte prosecutors weigh dropping bribery article
World.content:
Vice President Sara Duterte arrives at the Senate of the Philippines, Pasay City in this file photo taken on July 7, 2026. INQUIRER PHOTO / NIÑO JESUS ORBETA

MANILA, Philippines — House prosecutors have not made a final decision on whether to drop the bribery article against Vice President Sara Duterte as they consider ways to speed up her impeachment trial, private prosecutor Benjamin “Jay” Tolosa Jr. said Saturday.

Tolosa said prosecutors were reviewing the article alongside their remaining witnesses as part of efforts to finish the trial sooner and avoid extending the proceedings into next year.

“We always say that we don’t want this to extend into next year,” Tolosa said at the Saturday News Forum at Dapo Restaurant in Quezon City.

Article continues after this 

Article III concerns alleged bribery involving Department of Education officials during Duterte’s term as education secretary. Prosecutors had publicly raised the possibility of dropping the article earlier in the week.

Tolosa said prosecutors shared the desire expressed by members of the public and some senator-judges for a faster trial. The panel was reviewing the evidence that still needed to be presented and the number of witnesses necessary to establish its case.

He cited the prosecution’s presentation on grave threats, saying it stopped calling additional witnesses after determining that the evidence it sought to establish had already been presented.

“There were so many witnesses whom we no longer called,” Tolosa said. “When we felt that we were able to meet them already, we stopped there.”

Tolosa said prosecutors had planned to take the same approach when they began presenting evidence concerning confidential funds by reducing the number of witnesses once the necessary testimony had been given.

Article continues after this 

“And we said from the very start of this discussion on confidential funds that we also wanted, as much as possible, to considerably trim down our witness list,” he said.

The review of Article III is part of that effort, Tolosa said. Prosecutors were considering whether foregoing the presentation of evidence on the article could help shorten the trial.

Article continues after this 

His remarks followed lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro’s Sept. 3 statement that the panel was reviewing the bribery article and its remaining witnesses, with no final decision yet on dropping the article.

Tolosa said there was precedent for narrowing an impeachment case, citing the 2012 trial of the late Chief Justice Renato Corona, when prosecutors withdrew five of the eight impeachment articles.

World.title: DA in Davao signs deals to bring Saba bananas to Hong Kong, New Zealand
World.content:
Saba bananas growm in Davao Region (PNA file photo)

DAVAO CITY — The Department of Agriculture in Davao Region (DA-11) announced Friday that Philippine Saba (Cardava) bananas are set to reach new international markets.

This development comes following the signing of two Supply and Purchase Agreements during Asia Fruit Logistica Hong Kong 2026 on Sept. 2.

Last month, an initial 20-ton shipment of Cardava bananas bound for Saudi Arabia was sent by accredited exporter GERB Golden Hands Corp.

Article continues after this

DA-11 said the new agreements were signed between Philippine exporter Avante Agri-Products Philippines Inc. and Cozy and Korner Trading Co. of Hong Kong, as well as Fresh Produce Group (FPG) Ltd. of New Zealand.

Cozy and Korner will serve as the exclusive distributor in Hong Kong, while FPG Ltd. will act as the exclusive importer and distributor in New Zealand.

“The new agreement strengthens trade linkages between Philippine exporters and international buyers and creates new market opportunities for Philippine agricultural products, particularly premium export-quality Saba bananas,” DA-11 said in a statement.

The signing was among the highlights of the Philippines’ participation in AFL 2026, where DA led a delegation of fruit industry associations to promote local produce and explore new international markets.

Article continues after this 

Meanwhile, DA-11 also reported its participation in the Sabah International Expo 2026 (SIE 2026), a biennial trade fair in Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia, running from Sept. 2–6.

The expo serves as a platform for exhibitors across the Brunei Darussalam–Indonesia–Malaysia–Philippines East ASEAN Growth Area (BIMP-EAGA) and ASEAN.

Article continues after this 

DA-11 Regional Technical Director for Operations Marie Ann Constantino said the participation highlights the competitiveness of Philippine products, particularly those from Davao Region, while opening opportunities for Halal-certified enterprises.

“To access the global market, we must know and comply with the market protocols and requirements of the importing country,” Constantino noted.

World.title: DILG on Duterte: We didn’t arrest her despite knowing her location
World.content:
Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla (front). Behind him is PNP Chief Jose Melencio Nartatez. (File photo)

MANILA, Philippines — Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Saturday said they already knew Vice President Sara Duterte’s whereabouts, but chose not to “force the warrant of arrest.”

“Its very unfortunate that all the pressure in her life is affecting her perception,” Remulla told reporters in a message.

READ: Duterte: I was advised that posting bail is better than being detained

The statement followed Duterte’s remarks that she does not feel safe in police custody as she posted bail of P360,000 for three counts of grave threats early Saturday.

She also said that she feared for her and her family’s life as the administration had been pressuring and harassing her since 2023.

He said that the PNP has surveillance of her warrant being served until the vice president posted bail.

The secretary added that although they knew her location on the night after the Quezon City Regional Trial Court issued the arrest warrant, they did not act upon the order.

World.title: DepEd moves to strengthen Scouting policies in schools
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) is pushing to revise and strengthen school-based Scouting policies to make programs more inclusive, focused on character formation and responsive to learners’ current needs.

DepEd recently gathered Boy Scouts and Girl Scouts leaders and education partners for the Stakeholders’ Convergence on the Harmonization of Scouting Programs in Basic Education, where participants discussed revisions to guidelines under DepEd Order Nos. 76 and 86, series of 2012.

The convergence was held on Aug. 25.

Article continues after this 

Education Secretary Sonny Angara said Scouting provides learners with practical skills beyond classroom instruction.

“Scouting is not just a co-curricular activity; it is a cornerstone of character building. It’s about giving our learners practical tools like discipline, teamwork, and crisis management that ground them for life and directly enrich what they learn in class,” Angara said.

“We are modernizing these policies to ensure every learner gains access to real-world leadership skills, resilience, and a strong sense of civic duty in a safe, supportive environment,” he added.

DepEd said the initiative is aligned with its Quality Basic Education Development Plan and Five-Point Reform Agenda.

The agency considers Scouting a co-curricular activity that can help develop character, leadership and community service while supporting learners’ physical and mental well-being and curbing school-based violence.

Article continues after this 

The policy review is also part of broader DepEd reforms intended to protect schools from learning disruptions and safety risks.

Officials from the Boy Scouts of the Philippines (BSP), Girl Scouts of the Philippines (GSP), Ten Outstanding Boy Scouts of the Philippines, Chief Girl Scout Medalists, Association of Top Achievers Scout–Philippine Chapter and National Eagle Scouts Association of the Philippines attended the convergence.

Article continues after this 

Representatives from the National Youth Commission and National Federation of Supreme Secondary Learner Government, as well as veteran DepEd Scouting advisers, also participated.

BSP Senior Vice President Jose Mari G. Pelaez said challenges encountered in implementing Scouting programs in schools underscored the need to update existing policies.

Pelaez also emphasized the long-standing partnership between DepEd and Scouting organizations in providing activities aimed at developing well-rounded learners.

GSP National President Cristina Lim-Yuson, meanwhile, said collaboration among DepEd and community partners helps ensure that education goes beyond academics to develop confident, resilient, compassionate and active learners.

Lim-Yuson said the initiative was not merely about funding but also about shared responsibility, with schools identifying learners’ needs and partner organizations providing the necessary resources and training.

Participants agreed to promote Scouting as a leading co-curricular activity for building character and fostering peace and safety inside and outside schools.

World.title: Angara honors 2 teachers in 2026 Outstanding Filipinos awards
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines — Education Secretary Sonny Angara honored two public school teachers at the 2026 Metrobank Foundation Outstanding Filipinos awards on Friday for their leadership and compassionate teaching in basic education.

Angara co-presented the awards with Metrobank senior management, highlighting the work of educators who go beyond their duties to help their students and communities.

“Our teachers are the heart and foundation of our education system. What Dr. Emmanuel Guarde and Engr. Sheila Marie Amigo have demonstrated proves that when a teacher’s love extends beyond the classroom, an entire community can be transformed and uplifted,” Angara said, translated from Filipino.

Article continues after this 

Citing President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s directive to care for teachers and improve basic education, Angara said the awardees served as “steady beacons of hope, compassion, and innovation.”

“They remind us every day that behind every child who dreams is a teacher who first believed in them, sacrificed for them, and gave them the tools to succeed,” he added.

Guarde, a Master Teacher III at Cornelio Lintawagin Memorial Elementary School in Naujan, Oriental Mindoro, is a member of the Alangan Mangyan indigenous community who has spent 17 years promoting culture-based education.

He developed localized early-grade learning resources and the Mangyan Alangan Community-Based Competencies framework. He also helped establish a primary school, solar lighting and basic facilities in the remote community of Sitio Begnay.

Guarde also initiated the Adult Education and Livelihood Strategy Management Plan, which provides community members with functional literacy and vocational skills.

Article continues after this 

“I believe that quality education must be both accessible and meaningful,” Guarde said.

“Through my extensive research on the traditions and values of the Alangan Mangyan, I seek to contribute to the integration of indigenous knowledge into the curriculum so that education can become more inclusive, relevant, and respectful of cultural diversity,” he added.

Article continues after this 

Amigo, a Master Teacher I and licensed electrical engineer at Siay National High School in Siay, Zamboanga Sibugay, has served for 11 years.

She developed DULA, or Dynamic Utilization of Learning by Amusement, an initiative that uses low-cost, hands-on learning tools to make science more accessible to high school students.

Through the initiative, students’ average test scores increased from 22.67 percent to a post-intervention average of 70.40 percent.

What started as a lesson plan concept later developed into an instructional strategy, with Amigo’s findings published in 2023 and gaining institutional support at the district and division levels.

Her DULA Eco Havens initiative also established hands-on learning spaces in local barangays.

“As an engineer, I used to find joy in designing systems and solving technical problems. But nothing compares to the immense joy of building a learner’s confidence,” Amigo said.

“My heart fills up whenever a student who used to hide at the back of the classroom out of fear suddenly smiles because they finally understand a difficult lesson,” she added.

Angara also reaffirmed the Department of Education’s commitment to supporting teachers through professional development and welfare initiatives.

Eight other public servants — two higher education professors, three military officers and three police officers — were also honored at the event.

Each awardee received a P1-million cash prize, the Metrobank Foundation “Flame” trophy and a Medallion of Excellence.

World.title: Abante wants Sara Duterte subpoenaed over P612.5-M confidential funds
World.content:
Sara Duterte_20260707NJO-5

MANILA, Philippines — Manila Rep. Bienvenido “Benny” Abante Jr. on Friday called for Vice President Sara Duterte to be subpoenaed in her impeachment trial to personally explain what happened to P612.5 million in confidential funds after witnesses disclaimed knowledge of how the money was ultimately spent.

Abante, chairperson of the House Committee on Human Rights and an endorser of one of the impeachment complaints against Duterte, said the Vice President should face the impeachment court herself rather than leave the task of answering the allegations to her subordinates and lawyers.

“The Vice President should really be subpoenaed now. She should personally appear,” Abante said during an online press briefing.

Article continues after this 

House impeachment team adviser and spokesperson Ace Barbers, meanwhile, said the evidence and unanswered questions surrounding the confidential funds ultimately point to Duterte.

“The allegations in this article have already been substantiated, but if there are questions about where the money really went, and all roads lead to Vice President Sara, then perhaps she should explain it to the people,” Barbers said.

Abante stressed that calling Duterte to testify would give her an opportunity to directly answer the allegations and would not amount to a presumption of guilt.

“This is good for the Vice President. It is also good for her because she will be able to answer all the allegations against her,” Abante said.

“And if she is subpoenaed, it does not mean she is guilty. We’re not actually saying that she is guilty,” he added.

Article continues after this 

Abante said he was personally among those pushing for Duterte to be called to testify.

“I’ll say it: I’m the one suggesting that she be summoned. Let’s go to the jugular. Let’s see. She is the impeachable officer, so she should really face the court,” he said.

Article continues after this 

Abante said there was little reason to continue relying on Duterte’s subordinates when the central questions concern her own accountability as the impeachable official.

“Let’s not make it harder for her deputies, her staff,” he said.

“Why? Because she is the only one who can actually answer all of those allegations against her,” he added.

The confidential fund article covers P500 million spent by the Office of the Vice President (OVP) in 2022 and 2023 and another P112.5 million spent by the Department of Education (DepEd) in 2023 when Duterte was education secretary.

Former OVP special disbursing officer Gina Acosta testified as a hostile prosecution witness that Duterte instructed her to turn over four P125-million tranches of confidential funds to then-security chief Colonel Raymund Dante Lachica.

Acosta said she had no personal knowledge of how the money was ultimately distributed after it was turned over to Lachica.

OVP Assistant Secretary and Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio similarly testified that only Duterte and Lachica knew how the confidential funds were implemented.

Former DepEd undersecretary, chief of staff and spokesperson Michael Wesley Poa, who is now part of Duterte’s defense team, likewise testified that he had no personal knowledge of DepEd’s confidential fund operations.

Barbers said the testimony left unanswered the central question of who actually knew where the money went.

“If you go back to everyone who appeared, none of them knew. The question is, who knows?” Barbers said.

“So who else could better explain where it was placed?” he added.

Barbers later summed up what he described as the unanswered questions arising from the prosecution’s presentation of evidence.

“Bigger questions have been left in the minds of our countrymen: Where is the money? Where is the proof of its proper use or the receipts? And third, who should be held accountable?” he said.

Barbers, however, stressed that the prosecution panel has made no final decision on whether to seek a subpoena for Duterte, saying the matter was still being discussed.

“We’re not at that point yet, and it is still being discussed. Someone is merely suggesting it. But there is no final decision yet on whether she will be summoned,” he said.

He said the prosecution could eventually ask the impeachment court to subpoena Duterte if her presence becomes necessary to resolve questions left unanswered by the evidence.

“If her presence is really required and the questions that are left hanging remain unanswered, perhaps that’s the time that we will ask the court to subpoena her,” Barbers said.

Barbers also acknowledged that the impeachment rules do not compel Duterte to personally attend the trial because she is represented by lawyers.

World.title: Duterte: I was advised that posting bail is better than being detained
World.content:
Vice President Sara Duterte arrives at the Quezon City Hall of Justice on Saturday, September 5, 2026, to post bail following an arrest warrant issued by Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 98. (Photo by GRIG C. MONTEGRANDE / INQUIRER.net)

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday said her lawyers advised her to post bail as this situation will be safer than being in police custody, following an arrest warrant issued against her.

The arrest order was in connection with the charges of three counts of grave threats filed against her in court.

“My lawyers spoke with me and advised me to post bail, instead of remaining in a separate confinement while in police custody,” she said in a statement posted on Facebook.

Article continues after this 

READ: Sara Duterte at QC Hall of Justice: ‘I don’t feel safe’

Her legal counsel further advised that it will be best to be protected by civilians who can watch her every move, instead of being isolated inside a detention cell, where her security will be less guaranteed.

Duterte said she has been pressured and harassed by the administration since 2023. She added that she feared for her mother and children’s security.

“I do not feel that my mother and children will be safe if I stayed with them, and I am deeply concerned about their safety and well-being,” she said.

Her statements came after the Quezon City Regional Trial Court (QC RTC) on Friday issued an arrest warrant against the vice president in relation to her reported threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez.

Article continues after this 

Her bail was set at P120,000 for each count.

Duterte, together with her lawyers Atty. Paul Lawrence Lim and Atty. Michael Poa, appeared before the QC RTC Branch 98 early Saturday to post bail, where she told the media how she feared for her life.

Article continues after this 

“My fears are shared by the majority of citizens,” Duterte said.

“They worry, not only about the safety of their families, their lives and their dignity, but also about their property and livelihoods, given the lack of adequate public services and rampant corruption,” she added. /apl

World.title: Kazakhstan to Host Its First Ever ICAO Aviation Security Week 2026 in October
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan will host ICAO Aviation Security Week for the first time on Oct. 20-22, bringing aviation regulators, industry leaders and security experts to the capital to address emerging threats and strengthen international cooperation.

Supported by Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Transport, the event will focus on the theme Safe Skies in a Complex World: Enhancing Aviation Security for All. ICAO Council President Toshiyuki Onuma, ICAO Secretary General Juan Carlos Salazar and senior representatives of foreign states and international organizations are expected to attend, the Civil Aviation Committee reported.

Kazakhstan reports 95.7% compliance with international aviation security standards, placing it among the world’s top 20 countries and making it a regional leader in Central Asia.

Security as a foundation for aviation growth

The forum comes as Kazakhstan seeks to strengthen its position as a Central Asian aviation hub, with safety and regulatory reliability increasingly viewed as essential to competitiveness.

“The long-term sustainability of a hub depends on trust in the system: trust in safety, regulation and predictable rules,” Civil Aviation Committee Chair Saltanat Tompiyeva said in an interview with The Astana Times.

Tompiyeva, who has worked in civil aviation since 1998 and was appointed an ICAO Global Ambassador earlier this year, identified Kazakhstan’s strong aviation security and safety record as a key competitive advantage. International assessments also show 82% effectiveness of aviation safety oversight.

Addressing emerging risks

The aviation security environment is changing rapidly, with new risks linked to artificial intelligence, cyberattacks, unmanned aircraft, critical infrastructure and geopolitical instability.

Aviation Security Week will address risk management, new technologies, workforce development and stronger information-sharing mechanisms, including approaches to aviation risk assessment in conflict situations.

Discussions will be held within the framework of ICAO initiatives such as the Global Aviation Security Plan (GASeP) and the Universal Security Audit Program – Continuous Monitoring Approach (USAP-CMA).

The Astana forum will also contribute to preparations for the Third High-Level Conference on Aviation Security (HLCAS/3) in 2027.

For Kazakhstan, hosting the global forum marks a step from regional cooperation toward a stronger role in international aviation security dialogue, supporting the country’s wider ambition to develop as a regional aviation hub.

World.title: Cyberport, Astana Hub Deepen Tech Ties Between Hong Kong and Kazakhstan
World.content:
HONG KONG – Cyberport digital technology hub sees its collaboration with Kazakhstan’s Astana Hub IT park as a two-way launchpad, enabling Hong Kong to expand into Central Asia’s growing AI market while offering Central Asian startups a direct corridor into mainland China and the broader Asia-Pacific region.

Cyberport Chairman Simon Chan said Cyberport and Astana Hub share similar development priorities, particularly in finance and information technology making the hub-to-hub partnership a platform for business expansion.

In June, Cyberport signed a memorandum of understanding with Central Asian’s largest innovation clusters Astana Hub and IT Park Uzbekistan during the visit of Hong Kong business delegation to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, led by Chief Executive John Lee. The partnership focuses on technology transfer, supporting tech companies in areas such as AI, fintech, smart city solutions and Web 3, and facilitating overseas expansion and global market access for innovation and technology companies from both regions.

“The finance sector as well as other sectors of the economy are growing fast in Kazakhstan. There’s also a lot of business opportunities. We hope through the collaboration, our companies, stakeholders and startups can open up the business there or find the collaboration with the Kazakh business entities. Astana Hub itself is comprehensive and focused on AI,” Mr. Chan said in an interview for this story.

“Hong Kong is one of the major Asian financial centers, not only Asian but also the international financial center. We hope to build Hong Kong into an international IT hub as well. And Kazakhstan is an ideal place for our companies to open up their businesses or make collaboration with the tech companies or financial companies for more collaboration and widen their scope of business and to seek more business opportunities,” he said.

Cyberport accommodates more than 2,300 companies, including 18 listed companies with a combined market capital of more than 500 billion HK dollars (US$63 billion), nine unicorns worth more than 150 billion HK dollars (US$19 billion). Its innovation ecosystem includes AI, data science, fintech, digital assets and blockchain, cybersecurity, and smart living.

In late August, Cyberport hosted the Digital Entertainment Leadership Forum (DELF 2026) marking this direction as a strategic one.

“DELF is important not only as an event but also its content is evolving every year along with the growth of different types of technology that can be reflected in its solutions. In the past, we focused on digital entertainment and other types of technology. But nowadays, we are focusing on AI and how to incorporate it in promoting the digital entertainment industry. We use this platform to reflect the development of different types of technology and attract guests from overseas to share with us and also to share their experience and insights with our local peers and stakeholders,” said Mr. Chan.

Building a global tech network

The Hong Kong SAR government has taken major steps aligning with the nation’s 15th five-year plan on positioning Hong Kong as a hub for innovative economy in the Asia-Pacific region.

The Cyberport chairman also spoke about the qualities they look for while building connections globally.

“We hope to build a gateway or platform for the different types of companies who can access different countries and industries. The critical success factor of locating a good collaborator or good competitors is the prospects for growth. The mission of the countries or the strategy of the development strategy of the country itself. In Kazakhstan, we have agreed to help make Kazakhstan more AI-oriented.”

Diversity in tech, talent development and different funding schemes for IT building up in Hong Kong are the main advantages.

“Hong Kong welcomes our friends from overseas to open up their office or presence here. We hope for more collaboration ahead. Collaboration is pretty important as the world is changing rapidly. We are looking for more hub-to-hub cooperation to build up more opportunities for the next generations,” said Mr. Chan.

World.title: News Digest: Foreign Media Highlight Kazakhstan’s China Ties, Middle Corridor and Political Reforms
World.content:
ASTANA – The Astana Times has selected articles from global media outlets covering Kazakhstan. This week’s foreign media digest highlights President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s vision for deeper Kazakhstan-China cooperation, the Middle Corridor, and more.

Tokayev links Kazakhstan-China partnership to wider vision for a more connected and cooperative Eurasia

Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has used the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek and a wide-ranging interview with China’s Xinhua news agency to set out a closely connected vision of Kazakhstan’s foreign policy – combining deeper economic and technological cooperation with China with a broader commitment to multilateralism, Eurasian connectivity and reform of global institutions, reported EU Reporter on Sept. 2.

Speaking as leaders gathered in Bishkek for the 26th meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) and its SCO Plus format, Tokayev presented Kazakhstan as both a committed regional partner and an increasingly active “middle power” seeking to bridge geopolitical divisions.

CPC: Total freight traffic volume along Middle Corridor increased ninefold compared to 2021

The Middle Corridor has demonstrated impressive growth dynamics in recent years, with total cargo volume transported along the route reaching 4.12 million tons by 2025, which is nine times higher than in 2021, Report informed on Sept. 1, citing an article by the Caspian Policy Center (CPC).

The author indicates that nearly all of this cargo flow passed through the Caspian Sea, making developed port infrastructure and adequate maritime capacity defining factors for the route’s viability. Delays at border crossing points and Caspian ports effectively caused an 8.4% drop in transport volumes in 2024, vividly demonstrating the acute need for infrastructure modernization.

Kazakhstan enters a new political era after historic parliamentary reform

Kazakhstan held its first parliamentary election on Aug. 23, electing 145 deputies to the country’s new Parliament, the Kurultai. The election followed a nationwide referendum in March, which approved a new Constitution that replaced Kazakhstan’s bicameral Parliament with the Kurultai. The new Constitution came into force on July 1, Euronews reported on Sept. 1.

The name of the new Parliament also had historical significance.

“Kurultai is a concept and a name that is characteristic of the steppe culture and Turkic civilisation. It reflects our national identity and shows respect for history,” said Nurgazy Anuarbekov, expert at the Kazakhstan Institute of Public Development.

President Tokayev highlights Singapore’s experience for new Astana International Airport

Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev discussed plans for a new modern airport in Astana and the use of Singapore’s aviation expertise during a meeting with Senior Minister of Singapore Lee Hsien Loong at Akorda, reported In Diplomacy on Sept. 1.

The discussion also covered political reforms, investment, transport and logistics, as well as cooperation in artificial intelligence and digitalization.

Kazakhstan completes connection section on key Middle Corridor railway line

Track connection has been completed on the Moyynty–Kyzylzhar railway line in Kazakhstan, which will become an important link in the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR or Middle Corridor), Trend reported on Sept. 3.

“The new 323.3-kilometer railway line will run through the Ulytau and Karagandy regions. Once commissioned, it will become an important link in the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR), also known as the Middle Corridor, improving regional connectivity and the efficiency of freight transportation,” the government said.

The project will shorten freight routes by 149 kilometers, reduce the load on the Moyynty-Zharyk railway section, increase the speed of container trains and expand capacity for freight and transit transportation. According to the approved schedule, the railway line is scheduled to be commissioned this year.

World.title: ChatGPT’s Kazakh Language Push Shows Why AI Must Go Beyond English
World.content:
ASTANA – ChatGPT’s growing development in the Kazakh language highlights a broader challenge for artificial intelligence: understanding a language also requires understanding the cultural context behind it, futurist and author Ron Immink told The Astana Times. Kazakhstan’s efforts to build Kazakh-language datasets and culturally specific AI benchmarks show why AI systems need to reflect the diversity of languages and cultures.

A joint project between the Qazaq Tili international association and OpenAI has developed a specialized AI Evaluation Benchmark Suite designed around the linguistic and cultural characteristics of Kazakh.

Developed originally in Kazakh rather than translated from English, the benchmark evaluates large language models on grammar, naturalness of speech, proverbs and fixed expressions, academic and literary translation, children’s literature, safety and ethnography. A separate 500-question benchmark tests knowledge of Kazakh history, traditions and culture.

The project also focuses on building the data foundation for Kazakh-language AI. The Kazakh Text Corpus has reached 14 billion tokens, covering different periods of language development and diaspora heritage, as well as education, science, technology, economics, law, medicine, history, ethnography, media and children’s content. Materials include text, audio and images.

Rauan Kenzhekhanuly, president of the Qazaq Tili international association, said during a Sept. 3 presentation that more than 10 billion tokens were initially collected from archives, museums, libraries and other sources after obtaining the necessary permissions.

The goal is to improve ChatGPT in Kazakh, including translation, information work and speech, text and audio recognition, while reducing culturally inaccurate responses.

Beyond English

The approach reflects Immink’s argument that AI development must account for cultural context.

“I think it is also going to be about context and culture. And I think we are definitely missing a trick. The problem is that most AIs are in English, but it should be in Navajo. It should be in hundreds of languages that we have. So it gets a much more deeper context,” he said.

Kazakhstan’s work demonstrates what this could mean in practice: developing AI in a language is not simply a translation exercise, but an effort to preserve the linguistic and cultural context carried by that language.

The initiative also complements Kazakhstan’s broader cooperation with OpenAI in education. Valerie Focke, OpenAI’s lead for education across Europe, the Middle East and Africa, described Kazakhstan as “a pioneer and early mover” in AI adoption and said the country was among the first globally to collaborate with OpenAI on the future of education.

As AI becomes increasingly embedded in education and everyday information access, ensuring that systems understand different languages and cultures could become important not only for technological development, but also for maintaining the digital representation of individual peoples and their cultural heritage.

World.title: EDB Launches PPP Scholarship Program at Eurasian National University
World.content:
ASTANA — The Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) has launched a scholarship program focused on public-private partnerships (PPPs) at the L.N. Gumilyov Eurasian National University (ENU), aiming to strengthen research, education and practical expertise in Kazakhstan’s PPP sector.

The initiative, unveiled on Sept. 4 alongside the opening of a new EDB-branded classroom at the university, is designed to support students interested in researching and developing PPP practices.

Under the program, students will compete for scholarships worth $600 to support their research. Recipients will also receive expert mentoring and have the opportunity to present their findings at EDB events across the bank’s member states, including the International EDB PPP Fellows Seminars.

The newly opened EDB classroom is equipped with modern multimedia technology. It will serve as a venue for lectures, seminars, project workshops, expert discussions and scientific conferences dedicated to PPPs and Eurasian integration.

“The EDB PPP scholarship program provides students with early professional orientation and helps them develop project analysis skills, while its international component enables comparative assessment of national PPP models across all EDB member states,” said Svetlana Maslova, EDB Director for PPP Projects.

“The program is designed to build a pool of specialists capable of preparing and implementing PPP projects both in Kazakhstan and across the Eurasian region. Students will gain not only academic knowledge but also a practical understanding of how real PPP projects are developed and implemented,” she added.

The Eurasian Development Bank is a multilateral development institution that finances investment projects across the Eurasian region. Since its establishment 20 years ago, the bank has focused on promoting economic integration and sustainable development among its member states.

As of the end of June 2026, the EDB’s cumulative portfolio included 348 projects with total investments of $22.1 billion. The bank’s investments are concentrated in transport infrastructure, digital systems, green energy, agriculture, industry and mechanical engineering, with a particular focus on projects that promote regional integration. Under its 2022–2026 strategy, the EDB is implementing three flagship initiatives: the Central Asian Water and Energy Complex, the Eurasian Transport Framework and the Eurasian Commodity Distribution Network.

World.title: National Bank Cuts Base Rate to 16.25% Amid Continued Disinflation
World.content:
ASTANA – The National Bank of Kazakhstan cut its base rate by 50 basis points to 16.25% on Sept. 4, as annual inflation fell below 10% after 11 consecutive months of disinflation. The regulator, however, warned that persistent inflation risks limit room for further easing.

“The balance of risks remains tilted towards inflation. Therefore, we are committed to maintaining moderately tight monetary conditions,” National Bank Governor Timur Suleimenov said.

Inflation continues to slow

Annual inflation declined to 9.8% in August, with food inflation at 9.5%, non-food inflation at 11.4% and services inflation at 8.9%. Monthly inflation remained at 0.6%, while core inflation stood at 0.7%.

Inflation expectations for the next 12 months fell to 12.1% in July, from 13.4% in June. Professional market participants continue to expect inflation of around 10% by the end of 2026.

The National Bank kept its 2026 inflation forecast at 9-11%, but raised its 2027 forecast to 6.5-8.5%, from 5.5-7.5%, citing higher external inflation, revised regulated-price assumptions and a stronger fiscal impulse.

Inflation is expected to stabilize near the 5% target in 2028.

“Our goal is not simply inflation below 10%. Our goal is sustainable and stable inflation of around 5% in 2028,” Suleimenov said.

Risks remain

The National Bank identified stronger domestic demand, fiscal stimulus, inflation expectations, fuel prices and utility tariffs among the main risks. External risks include higher global food and energy prices amid geopolitical tensions.

Tengenomika analytical Telegram channel described the decision as a continuation of easing rather than a shift to soft monetary policy.

“The National Bank continued the easing cycle. This is a normalization of the degree of tightness rather than a transition to a soft policy,” they said.

EconomyKZ.org analytical Telegram channel experts said the decision reflected a balance between declining inflation and still-strong domestic demand, with future decisions depending on whether disinflation continues.

Growth remains resilient

The National Bank maintained its 2026 GDP growth forecast at 4.5-5.5%. Kazakhstan’s economy grew 4.1% year-on-year in January-July, while non-mining GDP increased by an estimated 5.4%.

Investment in fixed capital rose 7.7%, while retail trade increased 4.1% in real terms. GDP growth is projected at 4.5% in 2027, while the 2028 forecast was raised to 4-5% from 3.5-4.5%.

The National Bank said further rate decisions would depend on inflation, domestic demand, inflation expectations, regulated prices and fiscal and quasi-fiscal stimulus.

The next scheduled decision on the base rate will be announced on Oct. 23.

World.title: Kazakhstan Completes Track Connection on Moiynty-Kyzylzhar Railway Line
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan has completed the track connection on the 323.3-kilometer Moiynty-Kyzylzhar railway line, marking a key milestone in one of the country’s major transport infrastructure projects.

The new line, being built across the Ulytau and Karagandy Regions, is designed to strengthen Kazakhstan’s transport and logistics potential, expand international routes and increase export and transit capacity.

Once commissioned, the line will become an important link of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, known as the Middle Corridor, improving regional connectivity and freight transportation efficiency.

The project will shorten freight routes by 149 kilometers, ease pressure on the Moiynty-Zharyk railway section, increase container train speeds and expand capacity for freight and transit traffic.

The project comes amid growing international attention to the need for expanded rail infrastructure along the Middle Corridor. According to experts, the pace of rail infrastructure development could have a “huge impact” on demand for freight rail services, while infrastructure development, coordination and supply-chain resilience remain key to the corridor’s long-term viability.

Construction is progressing according to schedule, with around 2,000 specialists and more than 700 units of equipment deployed at the site. The railway line is scheduled for commissioning this year.

World.title: Rights activist Siranush Sahakyan: ‘Lives of all Armenians held in Baku are in danger’
World.content:
Trials of Armenian prisoners in Baku

“The lives of all Armenians held in Baku are in danger. They may even express views that are contrary to their own will,” Siranush Sahakyan, who represents the interests of Armenian prisoners at the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR), told a news conference.

She said this was also reflected in statements dictated to the prisoners. Many of those who have returned to Armenia told human rights activists that they had signed documents under torture that “in no way reflected the information known to them”.

At the same time, Sahakyan said some prisoners express their views while “being prepared to face the consequences”. She specifically referred to statements from prison by Ruben Vardanyan, Davit Babayan and Davit Ishkhanyan.

“We should be cautious and attentive when analysing these statements. We need to understand whether they were dictated by the authorities in Baku or reflect the prisoners’ free will, because we cannot rule out coercion under torture. Those making these statements are simply in a situation where they have no choice. They are forced to make a statement under threat of reprisals,” the rights activist said.

Responding to questions from Armenian journalists, Sahakyan commented on the trials of Armenian prisoners held in Azerbaijan, described the conditions in which they are being held and detailed alleged violations of their rights.

According to official figures, 19 Armenian prisoners are being held in Baku, including former leaders of the self-proclaimed Nagorno-Karabakh Republic. On 5 February, an Azerbaijani court sentenced former President Arayik Harutyunyan, former Defence Army commander Levon Mnatsakanyan, deputy commander Davit Manukyan, parliament speaker Davit Ishkhanyan and Foreign Minister Davit Babayan to life imprisonment. Former presidents Arkadi Ghukasyan and Bako Sahakyan were sentenced to 20 years in prison. The lighter sentences for the two former presidents were attributed to their age. Under Azerbaijani law, people over the age of 65 cannot be sentenced to life imprisonment. The case of former State Minister Ruben Vardanyan was heard separately from those of the other former Nagorno-Karabakh leaders. On 17 February, he was sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Baku pursues ‘hostage diplomacy’

“The release of the prisoners requires, first and foremost, a political decision, since their detention itself was linked to the conflict,” Siranush Sahakyan said.

Siranush Sahakyan

She argues that resolving the conflict entails an obligation to release the detainees.

At the same time, she believes Azerbaijan is using the prisoners to pursue what she described as “hostage diplomacy”, treating them as a bargaining tool in the conflict settlement process.

According to the lawyer, this applies particularly to the former Karabakh leaders: “Holding them is particularly valuable in terms of hostage diplomacy.”

Charges not supported by any evidence

The representative of the Armenian prisoners at the European Court of Human Rights has not been able to examine the judgments in the cases of 15 of them.

“We only have an extract containing information about the charges and the sentences handed down to those convicted; it is not the full text,” she said.

However, she has access to the indictment and an English translation of the judgment in the case of former State Minister Ruben Vardanyan. The document runs to 3,302 pages.

Sahakyan has studied it and believes it demonstrates an unprecedented violation of the defendant’s rights:

“The entire trial was a farce and its outcome is illegitimate. We have submitted our arguments to the ECHR. Ruben Vardanyan’s case has already been assigned a number and will be considered by the court.”

According to the rights activist, the Azerbaijani authorities, “using an unknown methodology”, calculated the number of victims and declared that more than 18,000 people had been killed during the years of the conflict:

“And because Ruben Vardanyan joined this criminal organisation [meaning the NKR and its leadership] in 2022 and took up a position there, Vardanyan himself is held responsible for all these lives.”

The lawyer says Ruben Vardanyan is accused of crimes that have nothing to do with his activities or reality.

Moreover, according to her, the Baku court regarded the following as “criminal activity”:

implementing various social and charitable programmes in Karabakh,

renovating schools and kindergartens,

funding a large joint wedding for 250 couples.

His Aurora Humanitarian Initiative was also deemed to constitute activity linked to “terrorism”, while award recipients who visited Karabakh were described as members of a “criminal organisation”.

The Aurora Humanitarian Initiative is an international philanthropic project established on behalf of the survivors of the Armenian genocide of the early 20th century. Its founders are Ruben Vardanyan, Vartan Gregorian and Noubar Afeyan. They described the initiative as a gesture of gratitude to all those who sought to save the victims of the tragedy. Each year, the Aurora Prize is awarded to individuals and organisations that have “dedicated themselves to saving human lives and advancing humanitarian causes”.

“For example, one of the laureates is an Iraqi citizen. His receipt of a [monetary] award was classified as financing Iraqi Kurdish mercenaries,” Sahakyan said.

She stressed that Vardanyan’s case goes beyond the fate of one individual. In her view, it concerns the right to a fair trial, the quality of justice and the protection of fundamental human rights and democratic principles.

“The professional community has serious work ahead of it. It must not allow charges and convictions that have no evidentiary basis to become a precedent and standard practice,” the lawyer said.

Prisoners are isolated from outside world

The rights activist stressed that the Armenian prisoners held in Baku have no contact with the outside world:

“They do not see their relatives, consular officials, independent doctors, independent lawyers or representatives of the ICRC. In short, they are being held in conditions of complete isolation from the outside world.”

According to Sahakyan, their only means of communicating with family members is by telephone:

“However, all calls are monitored and permitted at the authorities’ discretion. Depending on their content, they may be forcibly terminated. The permitted frequency of calls also varies. For example, three prisoners are allowed to make a call once every 40 days, while the others are allowed to call once a week. The duration of calls also varies: two minutes, three minutes and, in some cases, 10 minutes.”

Some prisoners suffered fractures after beatings

According to Sahakyan, in recent months the prisoners have frequently spoken during telephone calls about health problems and a lack of medical care:

“After a certain hour, there are no medical staff at the facility. If emergency care is needed, there is no possibility of providing it. At most, they may be given medication to relieve certain symptoms.”

There have also been documented cases of prisoners suffering fractures as a result of beatings. The lawyer said she had information about which prisoners had sustained fractures but could not disclose their names.

Alleged torture over religious symbols

According to Siranush Sahakyan, religion also plays a role in the treatment of the prisoners, with such cases documented in international reports:

“Those who had cross tattoos had them burned, with the crosses removed from their skin through torture.”

She also said that although prisoners had been allowed a limited number of books, they were not permitted to receive copies of the Bible.

“There have been cases, which we have documented, in which they were forced to read the Koran,” the rights activist said.

Proposal by Ruben Vardanyan’s wife

Veronika Zonabend, the wife of former State Minister Ruben Vardanyan, has proposed creating an international women’s humanitarian delegation to travel to Baku in September. Zonabend hopes that a group of female human rights activists, under the auspices of Azerbaijan’s ombudsman, will be allowed to visit the Armenian prisoners and deliver personal belongings, photographs and letters to them.

However, it remains unclear whether the visit to Azerbaijan will take place. The proposal is currently being discussed with the Armenian authorities.

Sahakyan explained that because of visa requirements, security considerations and procedures governing access to prisons, the project could not be carried out as a private initiative.

Representatives of the relevant Armenian agencies have already met Veronika Zonabend and Vardanyan’s defence team.

“We have not yet received an official response. The matter is still under discussion,” Siranush Sahakyan said.

World.title: Drug for Duchenne muscular dystrophy to become available in Georgia early next week
World.content:
Givinostat for Duchenne muscular dystrophy to arrive in Georgia

According to Georgian Health Minister Mikheil Sarjveladze, the drug givinostat, used to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy, will arrive in Georgia early next week. He said all the necessary preparations have already been completed so that doctors can begin using the drug in the country as soon as possible.

“Today we have another piece of good news: we have received confirmation that the drug givinostat has been sent to Georgia by air mail. This means the medicine will arrive in Tbilisi by the beginning of next week.

We have carried out extensive preparations together with Italfarmaco. In particular, we have recorded patient data with the utmost accuracy, created a dedicated registry, approved the relevant regulations, and had foreign specialists train doctors. Everything is now ready to start using the drug in practice as soon as possible,” Sarjveladze said.

He said parents can call the ministry’s hotline for information and advice on how the medicine will be used.

Sarjveladze also spoke about another drug for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The ministry has been negotiating with its manufacturer in parallel with the talks on givinostat. The minister said he hoped the two sides would sign an agreement within days.

The drug in question is Elevidys, which doctors use to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

“In this case, I would like to share some good news with the public: we have completed negotiations on all the key commercial issues. We have already prepared and issued all the necessary legal acts on our side and confirmed that we are fully ready to sign the agreement.

We are now waiting for the company’s response and are confident that we will sign the procurement agreement for this medicine within days.

It is worth noting that the negotiations took longer than expected. This was mainly because of our firm position that we must clearly define and insure the responsibilities and obligations of the relevant parties regarding the quality of the medicine,” Sarjveladze explained.

The minister also thanked the parents of children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy for their active involvement in the process.

Background

On 31 July, Sarjveladze announced that the government would purchase givinostat for patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

Parents of children with the condition first met Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze on 3 June. After a second meeting on 4 June, Kobakhidze announced the creation of a working group to address the supply of the medicines the children need.

After the meeting, the parents said the authorities had agreed to provide the medicines. They expected two specific drugs to arrive in Georgia in about two months.

On 8 July, after meeting Health Minister Mikheil Sarjveladze, the parents said negotiations on making one of the drugs available in Georgia had reached the final stage. They added that they would announce details of the talks on the second drug the following week.

Duchenne muscular dystrophy is a rare genetic disorder that causes progressive muscle weakness and muscle damage. It mainly affects boys, with symptoms usually appearing in early childhood. As the disease progresses, it can also affect the respiratory and heart muscles. There is currently no cure, but treatment can slow the progression of the disease.

Givinostat for Duchenne muscular dystrophy to arrive in Georgia

World.title: Abkhazia to review how effectively agricultural grants are being spent
World.content:
The authorities in Abkhazia plan to review how agricultural grants have been spent. President Badra Gunba has ordered the government to return to the budget any money spent on ineffective projects.

The grants come from the Agriculture Ministry’s “Agricultural Development for 2025” programme and the Economy Ministry’s programme supporting small and medium-sized businesses.

The president’s decision to review how the grants are used was most likely prompted by numerous complaints from farmers on social media, who say the government is providing little or no support to actual producers.

Badra Gunba does not rule out some violations given the large amount of funding involved.

“If violations are found — and with such a huge amount of funding, they are bound to occur — we must respond to them. But most importantly, we should not simply punish those responsible. We must make sure they compensate the state for all the costs it has incurred and return the money to the budget,” the president said.

The opposition media outlet Respublika believes that the president’s decision to order law enforcement agencies to set up an interagency group to oversee state support programmes for small and medium-sized businesses can only mean one thing: something is clearly wrong with these programmes.

“It looks like someone has already decided to make a tidy profit from state support for entrepreneurs. Now law enforcement agencies have several options:

simply scare them so they stop stealing;

investigate what they have already managed to steal;

or get in on the deal themselves.

Which option do you think they will choose?” Respublika asks, making it clear that it believes the answer is obvious.

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

Agriculture in Abkhazia

World.title: Georgian businessman Elizbarashvili charged over alleged threats
World.content:
Elizbarashvili charged with making threats

Prosecutors have charged businessman and animal rights activist Tamaz Elizbarashvili, who is known for his outspoken criticism of the government, with making threats. He is accused of an offence under Article 151, Part 1 of the Criminal Code, which carries a maximum prison sentence of one year.

According to Elizbarashvili’s lawyer, Lekso Svimonishvili, seven alleged victims are involved in the case. Prosecutors say Elizbarashvili threatened them and that they regarded the threats as genuine.

Svimonishvili said his client categorically rejected the charges and maintained that he was completely innocent.

What do investigators accuse Elizbarashvili of?

According to the Georgian Prosecutor’s Office, an investigation by the Interior Ministry established that at around 2340 on 30 August, Tamaz Elizbarashvili and one of the alleged victims encountered each other by chance at a restaurant in Tbilisi. A verbal altercation broke out over a comment Elizbarashvili had previously posted on social media about the individual and his family.

According to investigators, during the altercation Elizbarashvili threatened the alleged victim and the people accompanying him. In particular, he allegedly said he would not let the matter rest and would return in about 30 minutes, while demanding that they remain at the restaurant.

“Since the alleged victims knew that Tamaz Elizbarashvili possessed a weapon that could be used against them, they had reasonable grounds to fear for their lives and safety and therefore decided to leave the restaurant.

At around 0020, Tamaz Elizbarashvili returned to the scene intending to carry out his threat. He was armed and attempted to enter the restaurant, conspicuously keeping his hand on a weapon tucked into his waistband. He also continued to threaten and insult the alleged victims. Those who had not managed to leave and remained near the restaurant had reasonable grounds to fear that the threat would be carried out.

Despite being barred by security staff, Tamaz Elizbarashvili nevertheless entered the restaurant premises. After establishing that the alleged victims were no longer there, he left,” the Prosecutor’s Office said.

What does the lawyer say?

According to Elizbarashvili’s lawyer, prosecutors cite comments previously made by the businessman on social media as the reason for the confrontation. However, the defence says the indictment makes no mention of any personal conflict between Elizbarashvili and the alleged victims.

“Mr Tamaz does not admit guilt, and his account of what happened is radically different [from the one presented]. During the incident, he left his wife and children at home to shield them from any potential confrontation and returned alone, believing that if anyone had questions, they could put them to him in person. However, no-one was there when he arrived,” Svimonishvili said.

The case materials also refer to a firearm, although Elizbarashvili denies possessing one illegally. According to his lawyer, he has not at this stage been charged with the illegal acquisition, possession or carrying of a firearm.

Svimonishvili said the only firearm seized during a search of Elizbarashvili’s apartment was officially registered in his name and had been sent for forensic examination.

The defence will ask the court not to impose any pre-trial restrictions on Elizbarashvili. Alternatively, the lawyer will request that he be released on bail.

Prosecutors have not yet specified what pre-trial measure they will ask the court to impose.

Background

On 1 September 2026, Elizbarashvili was placed under administrative arrest for allegedly failing to comply with a lawful police order. His arrest followed searches of his car and home conducted as part of an investigation launched under Articles 151 (threats) and 236 (illegal acquisition, possession and carrying of firearms) of the Criminal Code.

Elizbarashvili said the complaint against him had been filed by employees of the Imedi TV channel, with whom he had a verbal altercation at a restaurant on 30 August. He alleged that the Imedi employees had initiated the confrontation and threatened him over his political views.

World.title: Ex-Georgian PM questioned in prison over his statements on a human rights defender who died by suicide
World.content:
Georgia: Gharibashvili questioned in Jorbenadze case

As part of the ongoing investigation into the death of Lazare Jorbenadze, law enforcement officers questioned former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili at Prison No. 12 in Rustavi on September 3.

Jorbenadze had publicly criticised current Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze. Gharibashvili recently published a letter expressing doubts about the officially stated cause of the human rights defender’s death — suicide.

Following several hours of questioning, prosecutor Medea Tsiramua and Gharibashvili’s lawyer, Natia Tamazashvili, spoke to journalists.

Former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili was sentenced to five years in January 2026 for legalising illicit income on a particularly large scale. He pleaded guilty and reached a plea deal with the prosecution. On August 24, he was charged with a second offence — accepting a particularly large bribe. Gharibashvili denies the new charge.

What the lawyer and prosecutor said

How it started. On September 1, 2026, Irakli Gharibashvili published another letter from prison on social media, calling on government officials to answer questions about the true circumstances of Lazare Jorbenadze’s death. Gharibashvili pointed out that Jorbenadze, a former human rights defender, had criticised current Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze in an article by journalist Dito Chubinidze and died by suicide shortly after its publication. Gharibashvili also noted that the newspaper Asaval-Dasavali, where the article was published, had publicly questioned the suicide theory.

According to the prosecution, Gharibashvili’s public suspicions about the circumstances of Jorbenadze’s death have no direct factual basis. The prosecutor said the former prime minister provided investigators with no new or significant information.

She said the questioning showed that Gharibashvili was neither a direct witness to Jorbenadze’s death nor someone with specific information about it.

“Gharibashvili’s public letters were based solely on information from various publications, rather than any specific facts. He categorically stated that he has no specific information about Lazare Jorbenadze’s suicide,” prosecutor Medea Tsiramua said.

Gharibashvili’s lawyer, Natia Tamazashvili, who is his wife’s sister, said the former prime minister’s questions arose after he read specific publications while in prison and later learned of Jorbenadze’s death.

“His questions arose after he was sent a letter containing an article by journalist Dito Chubinidze in Asaval-Dasavali. The article was critical of Irakli Kobakhidze. Gharibashvili later learned about Jorbenadze’s death, put the facts together and raised questions publicly. During the questioning, he repeated the same questions he had raised in his public letter,” the lawyer said.

According to the defence, Gharibashvili was not trying to provide investigators with previously unknown sources or information. His questions were based on suspicions about a possible connection between the articles published in the media and Jorbenadze’s sudden death.

Series of interrogations in the Lazare Jorbenadze case

Before Gharibashvili was questioned, politicians and public figures were questioned at the Digomi police headquarters in Tbilisi. They were asked about the former prime minister’s letter published on social media.

Investigators questioned Nika Gvaramia, one of the leaders of the opposition coalition For Change, analyst Gia Khukhashvili and several activists.

Gvaramia said he had no information about the details of the case and knew only what had been published on social media.

Opposition politicians Khatia Dekanoidze and Tazo Datunashvili, as well as journalist Nanuka Zhorzholiani, refused to appear for questioning at the police station. They told investigators they would give evidence only in court, in the presence of a magistrate judge.

World.title: ‘If Russia decides to withdraw its military base, we will not object’ – Pashinyan
World.content:
Pashinyan on the withdrawal of Russia’s military base from Armenia.

“If Russia decides to withdraw its military base from Armenia, we will not object. But if they want to stay, we are ready to discuss that too,” Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said during his regular weekly briefing.

He also said Yerevan does not consider the presence of Russia’s 102nd military base in Armenia vital.

Putin raised the issue after his meeting with Pashinyan in Bishkek, although the Armenian prime minister says they did not discuss the issue either during those talks or before them. Putin said:

“If Armenia believes that Russia’s military base is not needed in Armenia, we will leave tomorrow if necessary. Is Armenia ready for that? Fine, we will not impose anything on anyone. But if the Armenian people want some kind of Russian military ‘wing’ there, we will stay. We will work and cooperate.”

Pashinyan also commented at the briefing on the issues he discussed with Putin in Bishkek. In particular, he once again explained Armenia’s position on its membership in the Russian-led Eurasian Economic Union, Russia’s concession to operate Armenia’s railways and the construction of a new nuclear power plant.

Armenia cannot be forced to hold a referendum

“And who said that all EAEU member states swore allegiance and would remain members of the EAEU for their entire existence?”

That was Pashinyan’s answer to a question about Armenia’s membership in the Russian-led EAEU. He gave it among the first answers at the briefing. The issue also dominated the open part of the Pashinyan-Putin talks.

For several months, Russia has been calling at various levels for Armenia to hold a referendum on membership of the EAEU or the European Union. The Russian president also insisted on this at the meeting in Bishkek.

“The adoption of the law to begin Armenia’s accession to another organisation amounts to a declaration that it is leaving ours,”* Putin said.

Pashinyan explained to the Russian president, and repeated at the briefing, that under the union’s charter, a country must give six months’ notice before ending its membership. However, Armenia has no such intention for now.

He said he continues to explain this to his Russian partners, trying to make Armenia’s position “clearer and more acceptable”.

One journalist who raised the issue described Putin’s tone towards Pashinyan as “harsh”. He said Moscow was taking a tough line and forcing Yerevan to choose between the EAEU and the EU. Armenia’s prime minister replied:

“I am also giving the Russian president a tough choice. I say: this cannot continue, the issue of the railway concession must be resolved. Why is there no headline saying ‘Pashinyan gives Russian president a tough choice’?”

Pashinyan himself believes Armenian media do not use such headlines because the country still follows the “logic of subordination to the Central Committee of the USSR”. In his view, that logic produces the following reaction: “They called from Moscow, we urgently need to bring out the cognac.”

At the same time, the prime minister stressed his position: Armenia cannot be forced to hold a referendum.

He said the country’s Constitution requires a referendum before joining a supranational organisation. However, Armenia should hold one only when the issue “is ripe”. This would mean, in particular, when Armenia applies for EU membership or at least sets out its roadmap. Holding a referendum before that, he argued, would mean asking citizens to go to polling stations before anyone has formulated the question or decided what answers they can choose.

Selling the railway concession is the best solution

Pashinyan said he discussed the future of South Caucasus Railway with Putin. This issue is, incidentally, more important to the Armenian side. For a long time, Armenia’s authorities have been telling their Russian partners that the country is losing its competitive advantage in developing regional railway links because Russia controls the Armenian railway.

Since 2008, the company South Caucasus Railway has operated Armenia’s railway under a concession agreement. Russian Railways owns 100% of the company. The agreement grants the concession for 30 years. However, since 2008, freight traffic on Armenia’s railways has halved, some routes have stopped operating, and the investment commitments have remained unfulfilled.

The Armenian prime minister therefore proposed selling the concession to a third country that is friendly to both Armenia and Russia. Russian partners described the proposal as “strange and largely unacceptable”.

However, Pashinyan said the following about the outcome of his meeting with Putin:

“We reached an understanding that the current situation cannot continue for much longer. We need to resolve this issue somehow. Both Armenia and Russia understand that one possible solution would be to sell the concession rights to a third party acceptable to both Armenia and Russia. Frankly, I think this is the best solution. The other options seem unrealistic.”».

Moscow to present proposals for building a new nuclear power plant

According to Pashinyan, Rosatom CEO Alexei Likhachev will visit Armenia in September.

“He will present Armenia with proposals on what Russia can offer today for the construction of a new nuclear power plant. I have already said that we do not see the nuclear power plant as a geopolitical choice. We need the best value for money. We will go with whoever makes the best offer,” the prime minister said.

He said Armenia would consider all possible options, whether a small modular reactor proposed by Western partners or a conventional Russian nuclear power plant:

“We have never said that the Russian proposal cannot be the best one, including in terms of modular reactors. It is not the case that Russia has no proposal for modular reactors. However, there are a number of important factors: the price, the payback period, the construction time and the financing arrangements.”

Nikol Pashinyan said work on the issue had intensified and that Armenia should make a decision within a year.

He said Armenia initially favoured a small modular reactor, but “desire is one thing and reality is another”.

The problem is that experts are concerned about the lack of experience in building modular nuclear power plants and the potential risks.

According to the prime minister, if there are no operating or licensed modular nuclear power plants anywhere in the world when Armenia makes its decision, this will create “uncertainty” and make the decision very difficult.

At the same time, he said work was continuing to extend the operating life of the existing Metsamor nuclear power plant beyond 2036.

No plans to introduce visas for Russian citizens

Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said that “if Armenia suddenly introduces visas as well, it will not introduce them against us — it will introduce them against its own citizens”. She also said the move would affect Russian citizens who have relatives in Armenia.

Importantly, no one in Armenia had suggested introducing a visa regime for Russian citizens before her statement.

“We have absolutely no such intention, and never have. It has never even crossed our minds. We are very happy to welcome tourists from Russia. We can see that they have now become very active in promoting Armenia’s tourism attractions. Society also welcomes these people. And they themselves seem to feel quite comfortable in Armenia. We are happy to have them, just as we are happy to welcome tourists from other countries,” the prime minister said.

Pashinyan on the withdrawal of Russia’s military base from Armenia

World.title: Georgian politicians questioned after ex-prime minister’s claims about Lazare Jorbenadze’s death
World.content:
Death of Georgian human rights defender Lazare Jorbenadze

Georgian politicians have been summoned for questioning over public statements by former Georgian prime minister Irakli Garibashvili about the death of Lazare Jorbenadze.

According to the Georgian Prosecutor’s Office, investigators have confirmed the suicide theory without ambiguity following investigative work into Jorbenadze’s death on 4 April 2026 and interviews with members of his family.

Nevertheless, because convicted former prime minister Irakli Garibashvili and others have made public statements about the case, investigators will question several political figures further: Irakli Garibashvili himself, Nika Gvaramia, Irma Inashvili, Nanuka Zhorzholiani, Khatia Dekanoidze, Tazo Datunashvili, Gia Khukhashvili, Giorgi Liluashvili, Zaza Davitaia and Ermile Nemsadze.

What happened

On 1 September 2026, former Georgian prime minister Irakli Garibashvili published another letter from prison. He called on the authorities to answer questions about the circumstances surrounding the death of Lazare Jorbenadze, a human rights defender who had criticised Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze.

Garibashvili writes that Jorbenadze died by suicide shortly after journalist Dito Chubinidze published an article based on an interview with him.

The newspaper Asaval-Dasavali, which published the interview, questioned the suicide theory. In his letter, Garibashvili stresses that the public should receive an answer about the true cause of Jorbenadze’s death.

The former prime minister says he decided to speak publicly about the issue after comparing the contents of a letter he received from government representatives in February with other circumstances.



Lazare Jorbenadze

According to Garibashvili, on 12 February, officials acting on the instructions of Irakli Kobakhidze and Deputy Prime Minister Mamuka Mdinaradze gave him an article that the newspaper Asaval-Dasavali had published on 2 February 2026.

The article featured a conversation between Dito Chubinidze and Lazare Jorbenadze. Garibashvili says it focused mainly on criticism of Kobakhidze and serious allegations against him.

The former prime minister says the message he received suggested that he was behind the article. “I received a message expressing the suspicion — based on a completely false assumption — that I was behind the article in question,” Garibashvili writes.

Garibashvili says he categorically rejected the accusation and told government representatives that he had never engaged in publishing “commissioned articles”.

What do politicians say?

Khatia Dekanoidze, one of the leaders of the United National Movement, said she would appear in court to testify in the Lazare Jorbenadze case. She said Bidzina Ivanishvili bears responsibility for the system he created, so investigators should question him as well.

“Bidzina Ivanishvili created a system in which people fight for positions and money, testify against each other, fabricate cases and, of course, are deeply involved in corruption. That is why Bidzina Ivanishvili, Kobakhidze, Mdinaradze and everyone who fabricates all sorts of dirt for money should be summoned for questioning. As for the investigation itself, I have made my position clear: I will go to court,” Dekanoidze said.

Political analyst Gia Khukhashvili said he did not understand why authorities had summoned him for questioning in the Lazare Jorbenadze death case, as he had made no specific statements about Jorbenadze and only learned of his existence after his death.

“I only learned of Jorbenadze’s existence after his death. I did not comment specifically on the situation involving Jorbenadze. I spoke more broadly about suicide cases that raise questions. Kobakhidze and Mdinaradze should be here instead of me, because Garibashvili named them, but they are not being summoned — I am. And now this has turned into nothing more than a tragicomedy,” Khukhashvili commented.

According to Nika Gvaramia, leader of the Coalition for Change, investigators did not ask him about any other subjects during his questioning in the Jorbenadze death case. Gvaramia believes the case may serve two purposes: one could be political propaganda, while the other could involve bringing new charges against the former prime minister.

“The next step, I am sure, will be to bring new charges against Garibashvili, under the article concerning illegal wiretapping. As far as I know, investigators are currently questioning him in prison. Mdinaradze and Kobakhidze should themselves be concerned about such allegations if they are true, although Garibashvili should also provide further explanations,” Gvaramia said after the questioning.
