World.title: Social assistance is shrinking in Azerbaijan: Is poverty falling, or are low-income people losing support?
World.content:
Targeted social assistance in Azerbaijan

In Azerbaijan, the authorities have raised the income threshold for classifying families as low-income. It would be logical to expect this to increase both the number of people receiving assistance and the amount of support they receive. However, official statistics show the opposite trend: both the number of families receiving targeted state social assistance and the amount paid per person are falling.

According to the State Statistics Committee, as of 1 July, 349,300 people from 78,900 families received targeted social assistance. A year earlier, the system covered 353,300 people from 80,300 families. This means that over the year, the number of families receiving assistance fell by 1,400, while the number of recipients fell by 4,000.

The decline becomes even more striking over the longer term. In mid-2017, 498,400 people received this type of assistance. Over nine years, that figure fell by 149,100, or about 30%. Meanwhile, the country’s population increased during the same period.

These figures raise an important question: have the incomes of low-income families increased enough for them to no longer need social assistance, or has the system stopped reaching some people who still need support?

The income threshold has risen, but social assistance has fallen

Targeted social assistance is not a fixed payment. The authorities calculate it as the difference between the needs-based threshold for all family members and the family’s average monthly income. The calculation takes into account income from the previous 12 months.

In 2025, the needs-based threshold stood at 285 manats (approx. $167.65) per person. In 2026, the authorities raised it to 300 manats (approx. $176.50), an increase of 5.3%. Despite this, the average payment per person fell from 100.37 to 97.94 manats (approx. $59 to $57.70). In nominal terms, the payment fell by 2.43 manats (approx. $1.43), or 2.4%.

Applying the current formula to the average figures suggests that the system calculated recipients’ average monthly income per person at 184.63 manats (approx. $108.60) in 2025 and 202.06 manats (approx. $118.90) in 2026. This represents a nominal increase of 9.4%. Mathematically, the lower payments reflect the fact that, according to the system’s calculations, family incomes grew faster than the needs-based threshold.

However, these figures do not prove that the financial situation of all low-income families has improved. The average for families that remained in the system in mid-2026 is being compared with the average for families that received assistance a year earlier. Families whose payments stopped or whose applications were rejected no longer form part of the new average.

Our calculations, based on official data, show that total monthly payments to recipients fell from about 35.46 million (approx. $20.86 million) to 34.21 million manats (approx. $20.12 million). The government therefore reduced its monthly spending on this group by about 1.25 million manats (approx. $735,300), or 3.5%, in nominal terms.

The assistance has lost even more purchasing power

According to July 2026 data, annual inflation stood at 5.8%, while food inflation reached 7.3%. After taking price rises into account, the purchasing power of the 97.94-manat payment fell by about 7.8% compared with the 100.37-manat payment a year earlier. If we consider only food price increases, the decline approaches 9%.

After receiving assistance, the system brings a family’s calculated income per person up to the needs-based threshold of 300 manats. However, this represents only a 5.3% increase from last year’s level of 285 manats. That increase falls short of overall inflation and especially of food price growth. As a result, even the minimum income of families that remain in the social assistance system has not increased in real terms.

The number of people receiving assistance is not the number of people living in poverty

The State Statistics Committee’s final data for 2025 put the poverty line at 286 manats (approx. $168.20) and the poverty rate at 5.2%. With a population of 10.26 million, this amounts to roughly 534,000 people.

At the end of the same year, 336,000 people received targeted social assistance, or about 3.3% of the population. The authorities use different methodologies and reporting dates to calculate these figures, so we cannot directly compare them. Nevertheless, the gap of about 198,000 people clearly shows that the number of assistance recipients cannot serve as a measure of poverty in the country.

Moreover, earning less than 300 manats does not in itself qualify a person for assistance. Under the rules, a family must show that factors beyond its control have caused its low income. The official criteria allow authorities to reject an application if the family owns or uses a car, has two properties of the same type at different addresses, or has carried out purchase or sale transactions worth more than 12 times the subsistence minimum over the previous 12 months. Authorities can also reject an application if an able-bodied family member has turned down two suitable job offers.

Based on the 2026 subsistence minimum, the threshold for purchase and sale transactions stands at 3,600 manats (approx. $2,118). Authorities can also reject assistance if a family spends 45 manats (approx. $26.50) or more per person each month on utilities and communications. For a family of four, that amounts to 180 manats (approx. $106) in total. The authorities also count money and gifts from relatives, as well as estimated income from a household farm or garden, when calculating family income.

These criteria may help identify hidden income and assets. However, the same rules can exclude a family with a low cash income if it owns an old car, faces high utility bills or mainly survives on financial support from relatives.

The number of pensioners is falling, while more people receive age-related benefits

Another question arises when we examine other social security figures. On 1 July 2025, Azerbaijan had 1,103,300 pensioners. A year later, the figure had fallen to 1.1 million. At the same time, the average pension rose by 10.5% to 594.4 manats (approx. $350). However, the number of pensioners fell by 3,300.

Meanwhile, the number of people who do not qualify for a labour pension but receive a 220-manat age-related benefit (approx. $130) rose from 166,200 to 177,500. We cannot say that the changes in these two groups involve the same people. However, the fall in the number of pensioners as the elderly population grows, alongside the rise in recipients of a lower benefit, requires a separate explanation in terms of access to labour pensions.

What data the government should disclose

To treat a decline in the number of assistance recipients as evidence of falling poverty, we need more than one headline figure. The Ministry of Labour and Social Protection of the Population should report how many families entered the system over the past year, how many stopped receiving assistance, how many applicants faced rejection and why authorities rejected their applications.

The government should also report how many families failed to qualify under each criterion, including car ownership, purchase and sale transactions, utility costs, discrepancies in income data and refusal to accept an offered job. It should also disclose how many decisions authorities reviewed following complaints and what share of assistance recipients are children.

Without this data, we cannot conclude that poverty has fallen. So far, the official statistics show only this: the number of people covered by targeted social assistance has fallen, the average payment has declined in nominal terms, and its purchasing power has fallen even further.

Targeted social assistance in Azerbaijan

World.title: Azerbaijan tallies volume of Shimal-2 power plant energy production
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 5. The Shimal-2 power plant located in Baku produced 21.1 billion kWh of electricity from the date of its commissioning until September of this year.

This was announced in a statement from the Ministry of Energy.

According to the ministry, the Shimal-2 power plant was commissioned 7 years ago, on September 5, 2019.

The installed capacity of the steam-gas power plant is 400 MW.

Azerbaijan is implementing large-scale projects aimed at increasing electricity generation and diversifying its energy system. The development of renewable energy sources is a key priority of the country's energy strategy. Major investment projects to build solar and wind power plants are currently being implemented in Azerbaijan with bp, Masdar, ACWA Power, China Gezhouba Group Overseas Investment, SOCAR Green, and other partners.

As a result of these projects, thousands of megawatts of new generation capacity are expected to be added to Azerbaijan's energy mix in the coming years. This is expected to reduce domestic demand for natural gas and allow more gas to be exported.

According to Energy Minister Parviz Shahbazov, the share of renewable energy sources in Azerbaijan's energy mix is expected to reach about 43% by 2035 as a result of these projects.

The minister said Azerbaijan is implementing strategic projects to establish a new energy and investment platform between Central Asia and neighboring regions. One of the key initiatives, he said, is the Central Asia-Azerbaijan Green Energy Corridor project.

"The creation of a Trans-Caspian energy corridor that will connect the electricity systems of Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan is part of our countries' strategic vision," Shahbazov said. "This project also creates broad opportunities for developing the Middle Corridor, which will serve as a green energy bridge between Europe, Asia and China via the Caspian Sea."

According to the minister, the Green Corridor Alliance joint venture, based in Baku, is already operating and coordinating feasibility studies financed by the Asian Development Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.

Meanwhile, intensive work is continuing on the Caspian-Black Sea-Europe Green Energy Corridor, as well as the Azerbaijan-Türkiye-Europe and Azerbaijan-Georgia-Türkiye-Bulgaria energy interconnectors.

Shahbazov said green energy corridors are "shaping the geoeconomic map of the future" and that the initiatives will not only promote energy exports but also stimulate the development of digital connectivity, fiber-optic infrastructure and regional economic cooperation.

World.title: Azerbaijan set to undertake vice-chairmanship of LLDCs
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 5. Turkmenistan has been elected as the Chair of the Group of Landlocked Developing Countries (LLDCs) for 2027-2028, and Azerbaijan as its Vice-Chair.

This was announced by the press service of the Permanent Mission of Turkmenistan to the UN.

According to the report, its term of office will begin on January 1, 2027.

The report noted that the relevant decision was made at the meeting of the group held in New York at the level of permanent representatives to the UN.

Laos, Burundi, Chad, Rwanda, and Paraguay were also elected to the steering bureau from the regional groups.

This chairmanship will allow Turkmenistan to coordinate the activities of the group for two years, including work on energy and transport connectivity, which are priorities for the country, and to represent the interests of 32 landlocked developing countries, starting from January 1, 2027.

Besides, according to the report, the composition of the leadership will also be approved by the final declaration of the ministerial meeting on LLDCs to be held at the UN Headquarters in New York on September 24, 2026.

From November through December of this year, it's planned to prepare a draft roadmap for Turkmenistan's chairmanship of the group in 2027-2028, together with the Office of the UN High Representative for the Least Developed Countries, LLDCs and Small Island Developing States (OHRLLS).

World.title: EU’s Armenia decision: 80% concession and new double standard in S. Caucasus
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 4. The decision of the European Union (EU) to introduce new trade concessions for Armenian products may at first glance be presented as an economic support measure, but the essence of the issue should be assessed more broadly in terms of the competitive environment emerging in the South Caucasus, the principles of European foreign trade policy, and the influence of political factors on economic relations: by temporarily suspending import duties on products that account for about 80% of Armenia's exports, Brussels is giving Yerevan a significant advantage in the EU market, and thus rightfully raises the issue of equal competition for other countries in the region.

Real scale of 80% concession

On September 2, 2026, the EU Council supported the European Commission's proposal without changes, which envisages the introduction of temporary trade liberalization measures for Armenian goods. This decision allows for the liberalization of about 80% of Armenia's exports to the EU. At this stage, we are talking about the Council's position, and in order to quickly adopt the regulation, the European Parliament also approved the proposal without changes.

The measures must be applied within two years of the regulation coming into force. The concessions cover a wide range of products, including agricultural products, and tariff quotas are envisaged for some agricultural goods. According to official EU data, the products covered account for approximately 99% of Armenia's exports of fresh fruit, vegetables and plants to Russia, and more than 91% of its exports of beverages and alcoholic beverages. Brussels justifies this step by supporting the Armenian economy and diversifying the country's export markets. According to the EU, recent trade restrictions imposed by Russia have affected Armenia's exports and transit routes. One of the goals of the new mechanism is to mitigate these effects and further strengthen trade relations between the EU and Armenia.

It's here that assessing the issue solely in an economic framework isn't enough.

Political background of economic decision

The EU presents its decision as a response to the problems facing the Armenian economy. However, the political context of the decision is also quite clear. In a statement by the European Commission on July 2, 2026, Ursula von der Leyen emphasized that Armenia has chosen the path of reform and a closer partnership with the EU, and announced that duty-free access for 80% of the country’s exports was proposed, and an additional 52 million euros in financing was envisaged.

This point shows that Brussels’ economic policy is not completely separated from geopolitical priorities. It does not seem accidental that new economic opportunities are being created for Armenia against the backdrop of a change in its political course and rapprochement with Europe. Here, an economic instrument is being transformed into a means of strengthening political partnership.

This approach itself can be considered a legitimate political choice for the EU. However, the problem lies in the consequences this choice has for other economic actors in the South Caucasus. If economic relations are differentiated according to the level of political proximity, rather than by uniform and uniform principles, then it is not just about free competition.

Question of equal competition in South Caucasus

Against the backdrop of countries that have been trying to establish pragmatic and equal economic relations with the EU for years, pursue independent economic policies, and invest heavily in regional infrastructure projects, the creation of separate and large-scale trade preferences for a specific state raises questions in terms of regional competition.

Azerbaijan’s position is of particular importance at this point. Azerbaijan has long been building cooperation with Europe in energy, transport, logistics, investment, and other areas based on mutual interests. The country’s regional transport and energy infrastructure plays an important role in terms of Europe’s economic and energy security. In such circumstances, the question of how to protect the competitive opportunities of other regional economic partners when a large-scale preferential regime is applied to one country’s products is completely justified.

The point is not to object to Armenia gaining access to the European market. The expansion of each country’s access to new markets is a positive event from an economic perspective. The point is that the application of the same criteria is of fundamental importance for countries cooperating with the EU. Otherwise, political advantages begin to determine the place of natural competition in regional economic relations.

EU's Armenia policy deepens contradictions in region

Speaking about the issue, MP Mazahir Afandiyev told Trend that the EU considers relations with Armenia as one of the important directions of its policy in the South Caucasus.

According to the MP, various economic and political initiatives are being put forward to ensure that Armenia remains an important partner for the EU in regional policy. In this context, he focused on the implementation of preferential sales of Armenian locally produced products on the European market.

Afandiyev also considered the failure to take into account the relevant standards and requirements set by international organizations when exporting Armenian products to European markets as a noteworthy point. According to him, such cases can be considered, in a certain sense, as violations of the law and a double-standard approach.

He announced that the uncertainty over the direction in which Armenia's relations with its traditional partners will develop in the new geopolitical realities may somewhat delay the formation of Yerevan's final position on the TRIPP project and the taking of practical steps in this regard.

The MP also highlighted the impact of the EU's increased political and other support for Armenia against the backdrop of the geopolitical confrontation with Russia on regional processes. He emphasized that such an approach further deepens the existing geopolitical contradictions in the South Caucasus and, as a result, becomes one of the factors slowing down the process of ensuring sustainable peace.

Non-tariff barriers and different approaches are a problem

Access to the European market is not only about customs duties. Phytosanitary, technical, and environmental standards, rules of origin, and other non-tariff requirements can create a serious procedural and bureaucratic burden for exporting countries. The application of these standards is normally explained by consumer safety, product quality, and market protection.

However, the problem is not in the standards themselves, but in the absence of a unified approach to their application.

If strict technical, phytosanitary, and environmental requirements for the products of one country act as the main obstacle, while large-scale tariff concessions are provided to another country against the backdrop of political rapprochement, this raises the question of whether there are level-playing-field rules. In other words, there is a concern that non-tariff barriers serve more of a political filter function than an economic standard.

Here, it's particularly important to stress that the EU’s official decision does not mean that all requirements for Armenia have been lifted. On the contrary, the preferential regime is linked to certain conditions. Armenia must comply with the rules of origin, continue administrative cooperation with the EU, not introduce new trade restrictions on imports from the EU, and comply with the core elements of the EU-Armenia Comprehensive and Enhanced Partnership Agreement on democracy, the rule of law, and human rights. In addition, safeguard measures are envisaged to protect the EU market from possible negative impacts.

So, the issue is not about the complete elimination of technical standards, but about the political and economic context in which the preferential tariff regime will be established.

How sustainable “rescue” mechanism?

For Armenia, the temporary suspension of duties does not automatically prove that the country’s products fully comply with European standards. Tariff concessions and product compliance with quality and technical standards are two separate issues.

This mechanism can give Armenian exporters an additional price advantage in the EU market. However, the emergence of this advantage does not mean a fundamental change in the competitiveness of products. If the opportunities lost by the economy in other markets are compensated by new concessions, then it is possible to see a transitional support mechanism here rather than long-term and sustainable integration.

The fact that the EU itself calls the decision "temporary" is also an important indicator of this. The duration of the concessions is limited to 2 years, and they must be applied from the date of entry into force of the regulation.

On the one hand, this demonstrates Brussels' intention to provide operational assistance to the Armenian economy, and on the other hand, it shows that there is no talk of long-term and guaranteed market integration.

Two-year period and possibilities for political influence

The two-year period also raises another question: to what extent will a temporary economic concession depend on political relations?

If the preferential regime granted to a country is tied to certain political conditions, the economic advantage can also become an instrument of political influence. In this regard, the EU's concession can be seen not only as "market access," but also as a mechanism that promotes the political direction of the partnership. Brussels openly supports Armenia’s rapprochement with Europe. EU officials emphasize that Armenia has chosen reforms and closer cooperation, and link economic support to that political course.

Such an approach may be politically advantageous for the EU, but the precedent it sets is broader for the South Caucasus: if economic advantages take the form of rewarding political choices, the conditions of economic competition for states in the region are no longer determined solely by market indicators.

Why Azerbaijan’s position justified?

The logic of Azerbaijan’s objections or concerns is not about Armenia gaining access to the EU market. The main issue is an equal approach.

Azerbaijan acts as a partner that creates concrete economic value in its relations with Europe. The transportation of energy resources to Europe, the development of transport and logistics corridors, regional connectivity projects and mutual investments constitute the practical foundations of this cooperation. In such circumstances, the differentiation of economic opportunities by the EU in relation to the countries of the region based on political criteria naturally raises questions.

The principles of free trade and equal competition are tested precisely in such cases. In terms of the logic of free competition declared by the World Trade Organization, it's important to establish market access opportunities on transparent, predictable, and non-discriminatory principles. If the opening of a market is associated with political loyalty and geopolitical orientation, the discussion about a protectionist approach in economic relations becomes inevitable.

In this regard, the 80% concession that the EU wants to apply to Armenia is not just a technical issue of economic relations in the region. This decision also demonstrates what kind of partnership model Brussels promotes in the South Caucasus.

Issue not Armenia, but the same rules

The EU may have a political goal to help Armenia overcome its economic difficulties and gain new export markets, but at the same time, it must ensure that other EU partners have equal economic opportunities.

The two-year tariff concession, which covers approximately 80% of Armenia’s exports, will not go unnoticed in the competitive environment in the South Caucasus, especially since it applies to a wide range of products, including agricultural products and beverages. The fact that products covering approximately 99% of Armenia’s fresh fruit, vegetables, and herbs exports to Russia and more than 91% of its exports of beverages and alcoholic beverages are included in this mechanism makes the practical scale of the decision even clearer.

Azerbaijan’s position also proceeds from this reality: economic cooperation in the region should not become a political reward mechanism, and competition rules for countries participating in the same market should be as uniform as possible.

Otherwise, even if the concept of "free trade" is formally preserved, its essence may change in accordance with political choices. This is an issue that affects the economic interests of not only Azerbaijan, but the entire South Caucasus.

The main controversial aspect of the concession made by Brussels for Armenia is precisely this: it is not about helping a country, but about the principles of the assistance provision. If the main criterion for partnership in economic relations is not market principles, but geopolitical choices, then the demand for equal competition for countries like Azerbaijan, which pursue an independent economic and foreign policy, comes to the agenda quite rightly and reasonably.

World.title: Kazakhstan's Tokayev defines powers of Vice President
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 5. President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a decree defining the powers of the Vice President of Kazakhstan, the presidential press service said.

Under the decree, the Vice President ensures the development and submits to the President strategic initiatives in the areas of the country's domestic and foreign policy.

Upon the President's instruction, the Vice President represents him in interactions with the Kurultai, the Government and other state bodies, as well as political parties, public associations and international organizations.

The Vice President will also participate in international events upon the President's instruction, head the Secretariat of the Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions, and oversee the activities of the Kazakhstan Institute for Strategic Studies under the President.

The decree also assigns the Vice President responsibility for ensuring the activities of a number of commissions and councils, including those dealing with state awards, citizenship, state symbols and heraldry, training abroad, the Al-Farabi State Prize in Science and Technology, the Abai State Prize in Literature and Arts, as well as youth policy.

The Vice President also exercises other powers in accordance with instructions from the President.

In addition, the Vice President is authorized to issue orders and give instructions to central and local executive bodies on matters within his competence.

The Vice President may also attend sessions of the Kurultai, Government, Kazakhstan Halyk Kenesi and advisory bodies under the President, request and receive necessary information, documents and other materials from state bodies and officials on matters within his competence, and establish interagency working groups to draft presidential acts on matters within his competence and address other tasks assigned by the President.

The organizational, legal, information and analytical support for the Vice President's activities will be provided by the Presidential Administration.

The decree also approves amendments to certain acts of the President of Kazakhstan, as set out in the appendix to the decree.

The Government, Presidential Administration and Office of the President's Affairs will take the necessary measures to implement the decree.

The decree enters into force on the date of its signing. Erlan Karin currently serves as Kazakhstan's Vice President.

World.title: Engine flames from Sydney-bound Qantas flight forces plane to be diverted
World.content:
A Sydney-bound Qantas flight from Queenstown in New Zealand has been forced to divert as footage taken shortly after take-off appears to show flames shooting out from one side of the plane.

A spokesperson for the airline confirmed flight QF122 from Queenstown had experienced an incident mid-flight on Saturday, saying it was a "suspected engine issue", and had to be diverted.

"One of our flights to Sydney experienced a suspected engine issue after take-off from Queenstown this afternoon and the aircraft diverted to Christchurch," they said.

"Our pilots are highly trained to manage situations like this and the aircraft landed safely."

In footage provided to ABC News, the aircraft's left engine seems to be emitting flames.

Fight QF122 from Queenstown was due to land in Sydney at 4:50pm on Saturday. (Supplied: Liam Aspinall)

The Boeing aircraft had left the alpine ski town just before 3:30pm and was scheduled to land at Kingsford Smith Airport at 4:50pm.

The national carrier told the ABC that the aircraft was cleared for a priority landing at Christchurch, and both engines remained operating throughout, with no engine shutdown or failure experienced.

Liam Aspinall was sitting with friends having a drink in Queenstown when he noticed the flames approaching from a distance.

"I noticed flames appearing to come off the thing as it was approaching us from afar," Mr Aspinall told ABC News.

" Sounded like gunshots, [it] was loud. "

Support is being provided to passengers, according to the Qantas spokesperson, in recognition of what "would have been a distressing experience".

Passengers are being offered accommodation and help with getting alternative flights.

World.title: Two briefly detained over 'chaotic scenes' at Canberra junior AFL match
World.content:
Two people were briefly taken into custody at a junior AFL grand final in Canberra last night after reports of flares being set off and items thrown at players.

Officers were called to Phillip Oval around 8:30pm after receiving reports of a disturbance during the Under 18s AFL Canberra Grand Final between Marist College and the Belconnen Magpies.

"Reports received by police were that from a group of between 50 and 75 teens, items had been thrown at players, flares had been discharged, and multiple patrons were intoxicated," ACT Policing said in a statement.

"Two people were briefly taken into custody and released at the venue."

'Chaotic scenes' at conclusion of the match

Marist College deputy principal Liam Stakelum says the spectators briefly taken into custody were part of a group that displayed poor behaviour throughout the match. (Facebook: Marist College Canberra)

In a message to parents of Marist AFL players, the college's deputy principal Liam Stakelum said the end of the game was "chaotic", with spectators taken into custody for "anti-social behaviour".

"They were part of a group that exhibited considerably poor behaviour throughout the match," Mr Stakelum said.

"After [quarter] time, we made the decision to keep our students down one end to ensure they were safe and away from the potential risk.

" I will state that it does not look like these [spectators] were affiliated with Belconnen. "

ACT Policing said after the match concluded, event management staff advised all spectators to clear the venue.

"All patrons left the scene without further incident," the ACT Policing statement said.

ACT Policing confirmed two people were taken into custody before being released at the venue a short time later. (ABC News: Ian Cutmore)

Mr Stakelum said in his message to parents that officers believed the group posed a risk to students, and wanted to limit their engagement with the group as much as possible.

"I know the chaotic scenes at the conclusion of the match are hard to reconcile, but I do want everyone to know that the police were the ones who were in control," he said.

"The decision to remove everyone from the ground again was [made by] the police.

"This was done because they couldn't differentiate between the true Belconnen supporters, and the spectators who were causing the trouble.

"We may not agree with the decision, but coming from a safety perspective, I can understand the intent. Scenarios like this are not easy to manage."

An AFL spokesperson said the league worked closely with police to contain the situation and ensure the safe conduct of the game. (ABC News: Daniel Miles)

An AFL spokesperson said the safety of players, officials and spectators was "of paramount importance" to the AFL.

"[Safety] guided all decision-making during last night's U18s boys' grand final," the spokesperson said.

"The AFL worked closely with ACT Policing throughout the event and took appropriate steps to contain the situation and ensure the safe conduct of the match."

The Belconnen Magpies Football Club has been contacted for comment.

World.title: Five children in hospital after strong winds pick up two jumping castles
World.content:
Five children have been taken to hospital after jumping castles were picked up by winds in two separate incidents, in Victoria and New South Wales, on one day.

In Banksia, in Sydney's south, NSW Ambulance treated a boy and a girl for head injuries about 1pm, before taking them to Sydney Children's Hospital in a stable condition.

An infant with minor injuries was also hospitalised, and a woman was treated at the scene.

Just hours earlier, in Victoria's south-west, two children were taken to hospital after a jumping castle was lifted into the air, at a birthday party.

Victoria Police said the incident took place at a home in Lower Duneed Road in Mount Duneed, near Geelong, shortly before 11am.

"Two children were thrown from the jumping castle and taken to hospital by road," a spokesperson said.

"A large number of other children also playing on the jumping castle at the time escaped injury."

Ambulance Victoria said a mobile intensive care ambulance and advanced life support paramedics attended the scene.

"Two primary-school-aged children were transported to Geelong University Hospital, a boy and a girl both with upper body injuries in stable conditions," it said in a statement.



In December 2021, six children died and three others were seriously injured after a freak wind lifted a jumping castle into the air at a primary school in Devonport, Tasmania.

A coronial inquest into the Hillcrest tragedy will begin later this month.

World.title: Peter Katsambanis remembered as one of Liberal Party's 'finest' warriors
World.content:
Former MP Peter Katsambanis has been remembered as one of the Liberal Party's "fiercest and finest" warriors following his death, aged 60.

Mr Katsambanis served in the parliaments of Western Australia and Victoria, and was a prominent Greek Australian.

His wife Karalee Katsambanis said his family was "devastated" by his death.

"He was a great man: loved, adored, treasured and respected by so many people," she wrote in a tribute on social media.

"As his wife, I've lost my soulmate and love of my life and I thank everyone for all their support."

She also thanked the heart transplant team at The Alfred hospital who had been caring for him.

Peter Katsambanis is being remembered as the "fiercest and finest of warriors" for the Liberal Party's cause. (ABC News: Jessica Warriner)

Mr Katsambanis served in the WA parliament from 2013 to 2021, first in the Legislative Council and then in the Legislative Assembly as the member for Hillarys.

The seat had been a Liberal heartland before Mr Katsambanis was defeated by Caitlin Collins in Labor's landslide victory in the 2021 state election.

He had held the positions of opposition spokesperson for police, road safety, justice and industrial relations.

He was also a member of the Victorian parliament, from 1996 to 2002.

Liberals mourn loss

The Liberal Party of WA's state director Simon Morgan said Mr Katsambanis would be sorely missed.

"Peter Katsambanis was the fiercest and finest of warriors for the Liberal cause as a student, a trusted adviser and as a member of parliament in both Victoria and Western Australia," Mr Morgan said.

"Our party is poorer for his loss and we extend our heartfelt sympathies to Karalee and to all of Peter's children at this sad time."

Liberal Peter Katsambanis faces 'big challenge' to retain Hillarys Peter Katsambanis is facing a ''big challenge'' to prevent Labor's Caitlin Collins from wresting Hillarys from the Liberals.

WA Opposition Leader Basil Zempilas said Mr Katsambanis made an incredible contribution to the Liberal Party and to public life in two states.

"Service always came first for Peter, he was such a committed representative and he occupies a rare place in Australian politics, having served in the Victorian parliament and in both houses of the parliament of Western Australia," Mr Zempilas said.

"He will be greatly missed by his friends and former colleagues and we extend our very sincere condolences to Karalee and all the family."

Mr Zempilas also acknowledged his "significant contribution" to the Greek Australian community.

Mr Katsambanis served as president of the World Hellenic Inter-Parliamentary Association from 2017 to 2021.

He was also a vice-president of the Hellenic Community of Western Australia.

His family will provided details in the coming days for his funeral, which will be held in Melbourne.

World.title: Man on run after allegedly attacking three people with axe
World.content:
A man believed to be wielding an axe has allegedly attacked three people, including an elderly man and woman, in Gippsland and remains on the run, say Victoria Police.

Police were told the man, who is known to the victims, allegedly attacked the pair and another man at an address in Cowies Road, Tyers, about 12:30pm today.

The man, in his 50s, fled the address and the victims were able to call emergency services for help.

The elderly male and the second man were airlifted to hospital in Melbourne with life-threatening injuries, police said in a statement.

"The elderly woman also sustained critical injuries and was taken to hospital."

Police said a large-scale search was underway for the alleged offender, whom they believe may be armed with an axe and a handsaw.

He was last seen wearing a black-and-mustard-coloured jacket and carrying a black backpack.

Police said anyone who sees the man should not approach him, and instead contact Triple Zero (000).

Anyone with information has been urged to contact Crime Stoppers via 1800 333 000 or www.crimestoppersvic.com.au.

World.title: AFLW wrap: Suns rally after coaching spray, Roos maintain historic run
World.content:
Daisy D'Arcy has produced a dazzling display as Gold Coast's band of youngsters posted a three-point AFLW victory over Port Adelaide in a three-goal thriller.

D'Arcy racked up 34 disposals and 694m gained as the Suns, featuring nine first-year players, posted their second win of the season with a 2.5 (17) to 1.8 (14) victory.

Gemma Houghton scored Port Adelaide's only goal of the match at the 9-minute mark of the opening quarter, with the Power held to just six behinds for the rest of the match.

Sunny Lapin scored Gold Coast's first goal in the opening term with a nice effort on the run, but the Suns trailed until Havana Harris kicked truly at the 11-minute mark of the third quarter.

It would prove to be the match-winning goal, with neither side able to score a major in the final term as the blustery conditions took their toll.

Port had one final chance to win the match with 30 seconds remaining, but Gold Coast was able to spoil what looked set to be a certain mark.

D'Arcy was the standout player, but she received plenty of help from Niamh McLaughlin (24 disposals) and Charlie Rowbottom (22 disposals, 11 tackles).

Suns coach Rhyce Shaw gave a rare blast at quarter-time, and his side responded by scraping out the gritty win.

"We copped a spray, but that's what we need sometimes," D'Arcy told Fox Footy.

"The message was to go out and play our game of footy. Obviously the weather conditions meant it was going to be scrappy.

"The spray was to put our head down and get to it. I thought we did that well. I'm super proud of the girls to get the win and put the head down."

Abbey Dowrick racked up seven clearances from 15 disposals for Port, while Maria Moloney finished with 17 disposals, four clearances and 10 tackles.

The Power's Matilda Scholz was a force in the ruck with 15 disposals and 20 hitouts.

The result left both Gold Coast and Port with 2-2 records.

McDonald fires late as Bulldogs surge to stun Swans

Three final-quarter goals from young forward Emma McDonald inspired the Western Bulldogs to a soaring 27-point win over Sydney.

Emma McDonald kicked three goals in the final quarter to guide the Bulldogs to victory. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Jonathan DiMaggio)

Down by four points at three-quarter time, the Bulldogs surged home with the breeze by kicking five unanswered goals at the Whitten Oval to win 9.6 (60) to 5.3 (33).

After two behinds in the first three quarters, McDonald starred with three goals in the final term in a coming-of-age performance.

Rylie Wilcox also added a major in the last quarter to finish with three goals in a best-on-ground performance.

Runner-up in the last two Bulldogs' best-and-fairest counts, Wilcox had a game-high 26 disposals to go with her game-changing day in front of goal.

Coming off a thrashing by relentless back-to-back premiers North Melbourne, the Bulldogs had to overcome a burst from Swans superstar Chloe Molloy.

Down at half-time, the Swans hit the lead in the third term thanks to two goals from Molloy.

It was Sydney's first defeat of the season after it opened its campaign with big wins over Adelaide, Essendon and St Kilda.

But injuries have started to catch up with the Swans, who are missing high-profile recruit Taylor Smith for at least another two games.

Champion Kangaroos belt St Kilda

The all-conquering North Melbourne destroyed struggling St Kilda by 92 points for a record-extending 31st-consecutive victory.

The winless Saints registered the first behind of the match, but North predictably stepped up after that to win 14.15 (99) to 1.1 (7)

Having not lost since the 2023 grand final, the Kangaroos predictably condemned St Kilda to a fourth-straight defeat to open their season that will heap further pressure on coach Nick Dal Santo.

North spearhead Tahlia Randall starred with five goals, three coming in a second-half onslaught.

Veteran forward Kate Shierlaw finished with four goals, firing early with three in the first half.

Midfield maestros Ash Riddell (39 possessions, one goal) and Jasmine Garner (38, 11 clearances) were typically prolific, helping the Kangaroos dominate the clearances.

Ash Richards was St Kilda's sole goal-kicker, coming in the second quarter.

AAP

World.title: Melbourne soccer club says girls' match moved to make way for boys
World.content:
A Melbourne soccer club is taking a stand amid claims that one of its junior girls' team's matches was stopped at half-time, with players forced to take to an inferior pitch to make way for a boys' team.

In a statement on social media, the Boroondara Eagles Football Club said an under-12 girls' match at Caloola Reserve, in Oakleigh, was halted so that an under-11 boys' team could use the field.

"After a lengthy delay [40 minutes], the girls were directed to an alternative field that was substantially different to the original playing surface, waterlogged and unsafe, resulting in the match being abandoned," the club posted on Facebook.

The club said it was deeply concerned about the impact the July 12 incident had on its players, families and coaching staff.

" One of our young female coaches left the venue in tears, and many players and parents were left questioning why a girls' points match was not afforded the same protection and importance as the U11 boys fixture? "

The club has declined to participate in a rescheduled fixture against Monash City Villarreal FC scheduled for tomorrow.

It has asked Football Victoria (FV) to investigate the incident and clarify whether the events constituted gender discrimination under its policies and frameworks.

In a statement this morning, FV said it acknowledged the concerns raised and "the distress caused to the players, coaches and families involved".

"The matter is now being handled through FV's formal Member Protection process. To ensure it is considered fairly, FV can not comment further while that process is underway," the statement said.

"FV is also reviewing the expectations on clubs regarding match-day decisions, communication regarding abandonments, pitch use, fixture clashes and referee support to identify any improvements required.

"We remain committed to ensuring women and girls feel valued, respected and supported at every level of the game."

Father says players were discriminated against

Robert Stock, who was watching his daughter play on the day, said the situation was "so disappointing".

He said it was hard to imagine the reverse: if a boys' team was told to get off the pitch to make way for the girls.

"The girls on the day were discriminated against because they're girls, basically," he said.

Mr Stock said his daughter loved the camaraderie, friendship and fun of the sport, which was also teaching her resilience.

However, he was trying to keep her out of this particular situation.

"She's only 11. So does she need to know about gender discrimination this early?" he said.

The football club said on social media that it had lodged the matter with Football Australia's core integrity team, and with the City of Monash, which runs Caloola Reserve.



A statement from the City of Monash said the council "strongly supports women's and girls' sport and incentivises clubs that promote gender equity".

"Council has sought an explanation from Football Victoria as the governing body in charge of fixturing and match day referees," it said.

The Boroondara Eagles said they remained committed to respectful participation in football and the continued growth of the women's and girls' game.

"Our position is that no player should ever feel that their match, their team or their opportunity to participate is less important because they are girls."

World.title: AFL LIVE: Fagan lashes Lions, says Swans showed ‘human spirit’ in finals win; Dogs, Crows prepare in SA
World.content:
Many questions have been asked in relation to the Sydney Swans since that fateful Monday morning at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne three weeks ago.

Here’s one nobody bothered to ask: what happens if they actually win?

Logan McDonald of the Swans celebrates a goal. via Getty Images

Nobody bothered to ask because, before Saturday, the idea was preposterous. Outside of the Swans themselves, nobody genuinely thought they could win this game. Not a qualifying final against two-time reigning premiers Brisbane, who have lost only one game since May. Not without five of their best players. Not after everything that’s happened in the last month.

As soon as the Swans suspended the ‘Pullman Five’, a line was drawn through the club’s name by virtually the entire AFL industry. Their odds blew out with bookmakers and they sunk to the bottom of everyone’s finals power rankings.

Their own chairman, Andrew Pridham, seemed to think they were as good as done: their season had been “torpedoed”, in his words, when those season-ending bans were meted out to Isaac Heeney, Nick Blakey, Chad Warner, Riley Bice and James Jordon for breaching club standards. Even their own fans seemed to agree, with only 37,261 turning up at the SCG on Saturday afternoon. It was the Swans’ lowest finals crowd at home in more than a decade.

Perhaps the Lions believed it, too. Because only that could explain the way they turned up, as if they expected the Swans to simply roll over and accept their assigned fate. They did not.

And now, after Sydney’s stirring 53-point victory, one of the great AFL finals upsets, we are in uncharted territory: this crisis-torn football club is somehow just one win away from a grand final appearance, having absorbed every bit of angst and scrutiny directed their way and channelled it to their advantage.

“I’d be writing them off at your peril,” Alastair Clarkson said here two weeks ago in what proved to be one of his final utterances as North Melbourne coach. Prophetic words.

The Lions simply could not handle Sydney’s hunger, intent and efficiency, which overwhelmed Brisbane’s most celebrated names and punched massive holes in their much-vaunted defence. The Swans kicked six of the first seven goals of the match to leave the visitors stunned; that margin remained intact for practically the whole afternoon and proved to be the difference. They prevailed 21.15 (141) to 13.10 (88).

Kai Lohmann gets into a tangle with the Swans Getty Images

Every time Brisbane tried to reel them in, the swarming Swans had a response of some kind that kept alive the belief that was sustaining them. They simply wanted it more, whereas the Lions, having tasted the ultimate success twice before, resembled a champion boxer who got old overnight. Lachie Neale, the pre-eminent example, had just 18 disposals and two clearances, none of them important. Brisbane have overcome bad finals defeats before, but this one was a doozy.

Tom Papley started the day under an injury cloud after appearing to tweak his calf in the warm-up. He finished it with five goals, each of them somehow worth more than six points because of the energy he generated with his celebrations. Two came in a blitz at the end of the third quarter which pushed Sydney’s lead to a scarcely believable 46 points at three-quarter time, capped by Errol Gulden’s sensational individual effort from the centre bounce.

Logan McDonald produced the game of his career, bagging six goals. His first was the first of the match, and came at the end of a chain which featured a one-handed grab in the middle by Charlie Curnow over Darcy Gardiner. The last came from a set shot on the boundary in the dying moments. (Curnow also booted five.)

Charlie Curnow celebrates for the Swans. AFL Photos via Getty Images

Almost everything went right for the Swans. Almost. Something went very wrong midway through the opening term, when captain Callum Mills twisted his knee in ominous fashion as he tried to corral Will Ashcroft on the boundary line.

Confirmation that he would take no further part in the game suitably arrived, via the club’s X account, with a crying emoji at the end of the sentence as punctuation. Coach Dean Cox spoke about what losing the skipper to the team after the game.

“To lose your captain early, to rally, execute the roles they wanted to play at. I couldn’t be prouder,” Cox told Kayo Sports.

“We’ve worked hard on this game style for 10 months and we want to make sure that anyone that comes into the team can execute their role and do what is required, when it is required and they did that in spades.”

That Sydney still won without him, and after seeing his shattered visage on the big screen, further underlined the value of this performance. But a more cruel twist of fate was hard to imagine. Mills had risen to the moment as the Pullman scandal had demanded, leading admirably with both his words in press conferences and his actions on the field. He also missed Sydney’s last grand final appearance through injury in 2024; this was his first consistent season of football in three years.

In the absence of the five banned players, for all sorts of reasons, Mills was one of Sydney’s most important players.

Whatever they do next, they will almost certainly have to do in his absence. But you’d be crazy to put a limit on what that could be.

World.title: Swans v Lions player ratings: How the reigning premiers fared in their stunning Swans loss
World.content:
SportAFLAFL 2026 Opinion Swans v Lions player ratings: How the reigning premiers fared in their stunning Swans loss Scott Spits Sports writer and editor September 5, 2026 — 7:07pm

September 5, 2026 — 7:07pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Loading

No one gave the Swans a chance. Winning a qualifying final against the two-time reigning premiers was a hard enough task, let alone doing it without the five first-choice players serving a club-imposed suspension. What transpired at the SCG on Saturday afternoon was nothing short of remarkable, with the Lions dominated by 53 points and forced to enter a semi-final next week still licking their wounds. Scott Spits rates every Lions player’s performance from a stunning game. Brisbane Lions superstar Harris Andrews and Chris Fagan have plenty to sort through after their side’s stunning loss to the undermanned Swans. AFL Photos



Brisbane Lions (1) Kai Lohmann: He had a game to forget – a shocker, really. He didn’t bother the stats-markers until early in the second half and only had three possessions by the final break. 3/10 (2) Sam Draper: Very, very quiet. The big man couldn’t get in the game at all. A third-quarter goal saved a bit of face, but the Swans dominated around him that term. Draper badly misread a marking attempt in tough conditions in the second term. 4/10 (3) Jaspa Fletcher: Far from Brisbane’s worst, but he gave away an important free kick (for Sydney’s sixth goal) in the first quarter when he took the ball over the goal-line. 5.5/10 (4) Oscar Allen: The big man had a quirky kind of game. He did OK from limited opportunities and had three goals from three touches by the final break, and finished with four goals from six. 5/10



(5) Josh Dunkley: The midfield beast never stopped trying. He won plenty of the ball at the coalface, but had almost no one to turn to in the trenches with Lachie Neale and Cam Rayner among those well held. 7.5/10 (6) Hugh McCluggage: He just couldn’t get into the game and was largely ineffective. He had an early chance to kick the Lions’ first goal, but he was off-line. 6/10 (7) Jarrod Berry: He failed to have any real influence. Made one blunder in the second quarter when an errant handball went to Sydney’s Hayden McLean, who took his chance and booted a goal. 5/10 (8) Will Ashcroft: He largely battled in the first half but, to be fair, improved from there. There was one nice moment, in particular, in the first term when he stormed out of the centre and found Eric Hipwood. 5/10 Lachie Neale and the rest of the Brisbane Lions midfield had an uncharacteristically poor day. Getty Images



(9) Lachie Neale: Beaten by James Rowbottom, he didn’t touch the ball until the 20-minute mark of the first term. It was a tough day for Neale (by his usual high standards) and his team. To his credit, he still finished with 18 possessions. 4/10 (10) Levi Ashcroft: He struggled for influence. He booted what looked like a stirring goal on the quarter-time siren when his effort from an angle split the big sticks. But it was a classic false dawn as the Lions never really rallied. 4.5/10 (13) Logan Morris: He didn’t really have an influence, managing two goals from 14 touches. Brisbane badly needed a focal point, but he couldn’t offer it today. 4/10 (15) Dayne Zorko: Did his bit as teammates went missing around him. The veteran got better as the game wore on and finished with a team-high 26 touches. He was easily Brisbane’s best performer with metres gained (822), much more than any other teammate. 7/10 (16) Cam Rayner: Emblematic for the Lions on a shocking day for the two-time reigning premiers. He struggled to even reach double figures with possessions. There was one delightful pass to Conor McKenna in the third term, however. 5/10



The Swans lost captain Callum Mills in the first quarter, but went on to a big win over Dayne Zorko and the Lions. Getty Images (23) Charlie Cameron: The match-winning forward was completely unsighted, finally getting his hands on the ball in the second term but missing his shot at goal. He didn’t even pick up junk stats when the game was gone. 1/10 (26) Conor McKenna: He tried hard but just couldn’t get going. Had two touches for the first term as the Swans jumped them and had a vital goal assist in the third quarter when he kicked one off the ground to Berry. He also booted a final-quarter goal. 5/10 (27) Darcy Gardiner: He got smashed by Charlie Curnow and had an equal team-low four touches. He just had a shocker and the Coleman medallist took complete advantage. 2.5/10 (30) Eric Hipwood: Showed a bit at different stages and gave the Lions a target to kick to. But he was badly off target with a shot deep in the forward pocket after just eight minutes that failed to trouble the scorers. That didn’t help his cause. 4.5/10



View post on X (31) Harris Andrews: For one of the game’s best defenders, the leader of the Lions’ pack won’t look back on this game fondly. He was soundly beaten by Swan Logan McDonald, an opponent who had probably his best match and was a result-shaper. This one will burn for Andrews. 3/10 (32) Darcy Fort: He only played 50 per cent game time.
